Khairul Kabir Khokon is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Narsingdi-1. This BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) leader has become an MP for the second time. He is a joint secretary general of the BNP and president of the Narsingdi District BNP.

Khairul Kabir Khokon was born in Narsingdi District. His father is Md. Zahirul Haque and his mother Zahura Begum. He is a businessman by profession.

As a student he was the elected general secretary (GS) of the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU). He has long served as president of the Narsingdi District BNP. When the seat fell vacant on the death of MP Shamsuddin Ahmed Ishaq in 2005, he was elected MP from Narsingdi-1 for the first time in the by-election. In 2026 the Speaker of Parliament nominated him a member of the Senate of the University of Dhaka.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Narsingdi-1 with 161,405 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol. His wife, Shirin Sultana, is self-reliance affairs secretary of the BNP's central committee.
খোন্দকার আবু আশফাক ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Khondoker Abu Ashfaque is the member of parliament for Dhaka-1 (Dohar and Nawabganj Upazilas) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He is president of Dhaka District BNP and a member of the BNP National Executive Committee.

Abu Ashfaque was born on 8 August 1966 in Kalakopa village, Nawabganj Upazila, Dhaka District. He is the son of Abdul Alim Khandaker and Nurjahan Begum, and the sixth child in a family of seven brothers and one sister.

He passed the SSC from Nawabganj Pilot High School and the HSC in the first division from Dhaka College. He later obtained bachelor's and master's degrees from the Department of Statistics at the University of Dhaka. As a student he was elected VP (vice-president) of the Fazlul Huq Hall students' union at the University of Dhaka. He is a businessman by profession.

After his student days he served as a central assistant secretary of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and as president of Dhaka District Jubo Dal. He was elected chairman of Nawabganj Upazila Parishad in 2009 and re-elected to the same post in 2014. In 2016 he was elected general secretary of Dhaka District BNP, and later president of the district BNP.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as the BNP's nominated candidate with 173,781 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.

He is also active in social work. In 2005 he was convener of the centenary celebration committee of Nawabganj Pilot High School. He served as governor of District 315-A1 of Lions Clubs International in 2009-10 and as chairman of the Multiple District Council in 2011-12. He is married to Ismat Sakia and is the father of two daughters and a son.
গয়েশ্বর চন্দ্র রায় ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংস:
Goyasawar Chandra Roy is the member of parliament for Dhaka-3 (the Jinjira, Aganagar, Teghoria, Konda and Shubhadda unions of Keraniganj Upazila) in the 13th Parliament. He has been elected to Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He is a member of the BNP National Standing Committee and a former State Minister. In Parliament he is a member of the Business Advisory Committee and the Standing Committee on Privileges.

Goyasawar Chandra Roy was born on 1 November 1951 in Keraniganj, Dhaka District. He is the son of Jnanendra Chandra Roy and Sumati Roy. He is a farmer by profession.

As a student he was involved in progressive politics, and in the 1970s he was a member of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD). When Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal was formed in 1978 he joined it, and he later served as its general secretary. When the BNP formed the government after winning the 1991 election, he was appointed State Minister for the then Ministry of Environment and Forest under the technocrat quota. He was subsequently made a joint secretary general of the BNP and later a member of the party's standing committee. He had also received the BNP nomination for Dhaka-3 in the 2008 and 2018 elections.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as the BNP's nominated candidate with 99,163 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.
গাজী এনামুল হক ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে যশো:
Gazi Enamul Haque is the member of parliament (MP) in the 13th Parliament for Jashore-5 (Manirampur). This Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami leader is representing the seat in Parliament for the first time and is a member of the parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Commerce. By profession he is a lawyer of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, and he is also a writer and poet.

He was born in Potri village of Rohita union, Manirampur upazila, Jashore district. His father, Dr Mozammel Haque, was a physician by profession, and his mother is Mst. Nurjahan Begum. He is the second of ten siblings. After primary education at Smaranpur Government Primary School, he passed the secondary examination from Jhikargacha Badruddin Muslim High School in 1974 and the higher secondary from Jhikargacha Shahid Mashiur Rahman Degree College in 1982. He then obtained an LLB (Honours) in 1987 and an LLM in 1988 from the University of Dhaka.

Having received his Bangladesh Bar Council licence in 1991, he became a member of the Jashore District Bar Association in 1992. He has practised as a lawyer at the Supreme Court of Bangladesh since 1994. Since the 1970s he has regularly written poems, rhymes and songs. Several of his books have been published, and audio and video recordings of many Islamic songs he wrote and set to music have been released.

As a student he joined Islami Chhatra Shibir in 1980 and served as secretary of its Tejgaon thana unit in Dhaka. While living in Fazlul Huq Hall at the University of Dhaka, he stood for literary secretary in the 1991 DUCSU election. After finishing his studies he joined Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami in 1991 and became a rukon (full member) in 1992. He later served as a member of the Majlis-e-Shura and working council of the Jashore district Jamaat. He stood as a candidate in Keshabpur in 2001 and in the Manirampur upazila election in 2014.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026 he was elected MP for Jashore-5 with 132,876 votes under the scales symbol. In his personal life he is the father of four children.
গিয়াস উদ্দিন কাদের চৌধুরী ত্রয়োদশ জাতী:
Gias Uddin Quader Chowdhury is the member of parliament for Chattogram-6 (Raozan) in the 13th Parliament. This experienced politician of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has been elected member of parliament for the third time.

Gias Uddin Quader Chowdhury was born on 29 April 1953. He is the son of A.K.M. Fazlul Quader Chowdhury and Selima Quader Chowdhury. Alongside politics he is involved in business; he was a director of the family-owned QC Container Line Limited, QC Shipping Limited and Dhaka Dyeing.

He was first elected member of parliament for Chattogram-7 as the Jatiya Party candidate in the election to the 3rd Parliament in 1986. He later joined the BNP and was elected BNP member of parliament for Chattogram-6 in the election to the 7th Parliament in 1996. Within the party he has served as a vice-chairman of the BNP and as president of the Chattogram North district BNP.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-6 as the BNP candidate, winning 112,237 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
গোলাম মোহাম্মদ সিরাজ, যিনি জি এম সিরাজ ন:
Golam Mohammad Siraj, known as G M Siraj, is the member of parliament for Bogura-5, which consists of Sherpur and Dhunat upazilas, in the 13th Parliament. A veteran politician of the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party), he has now become a member of Parliament for the sixth time.

He was born on 15 January 1950 in the village of Dhankundi in Sherpur upazila, Bogura. His father's name is Golam Rabbani and his mother's Begum Setara Rabbani. He obtained a bachelor's degree from the University of Dhaka.

As a businessman, G M Siraj is the founder and chairman of SR Group. His companies provide employment for about ten thousand people across Dhaka and Bogura.

He was first elected MP from Bogura-5 in the election to the 5th Parliament on 27 February 1991. He then won the same seat in the elections to the 6th Parliament in February 1996, the 7th Parliament in June of the same year, and the 8th Parliament in 2001. In a by-election held on 24 June 2019 he was elected to the 11th Parliament from Bogura-6. In the party organisation, he took charge as convener of the Bogura district BNP on 15 May 2019. He is currently a member of the advisory council of the Bogura district BNP.

In the election to the 13th Parliament on 12 February 2026 he was elected with 248,841 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol. The Jamaat-e-Islami candidate for the seat, Md. Dabibur Rahman, received 143,329 votes. After the election he said that he does politics to establish people's rights and dignity. He named employment in Sherpur and Dhunat, fair prices for farm produce, education and healthcare as his priorities.
জয়নাল আবদিন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে ফেনী-:
Joynal Abdin is the member of parliament for Feni-2 (Feni Sadar upazila) in the 13th Parliament. Elected from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), this freedom fighter has come to Parliament for the fourth time. In political circles he is known as "VP Joynal". In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Land.

Joynal Abdin was born in Faleshwar village, Feni. His father, Chan Mia, was an official of the Assam Bengal Railway, and his mother is Ojibennesa. He is the youngest of five siblings. After passing the SSC from Feni Government Pilot High School and the HSC and BA from Feni Government College, he obtained an MA in political science from the University of Chittagong in 1976. In his working life, alongside business, he taught in the political science department of Sonaimuri College, Noakhali, in 1977.

He became active in politics as a student. Elected VP (vice-president) of the Feni College students' union in 1970, he became known as "VP Joynal". In 1971 he was elected president of the all-party Swadhin Bangla Chhatra Sangram Parishad (independent Bangla students' action council), and on 2 March he raised the flag of Bangladesh at Feni Government College. During the Liberation War he received military training at Dehradun in India and was appointed a district zonal commander of the BLF (Bangladesh Liberation Force).

When JASAD (Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal) was formed in 1972, he became a member of its central committee and the founding general secretary of its Feni district unit. In the 4th parliamentary election in 1988 he was elected a member of parliament for the first time, from Feni-2 for JASAD. He later joined BNP, served as general secretary of Feni district BNP from 1996 to 2009, and was again elected a member of parliament from the same seat in 2001 and 2008. In Parliament he was a member of the standing committees on the Ministries of Finance, Textiles, Works and Liberation War Affairs. He is an adviser to the BNP chairperson.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the fourth time, winning 131,210 votes in Feni-2 with the sheaf of paddy symbol. He is married to Shahana Akter, and the couple have two sons and two daughters.
জয়নুল আবদিন ফারুক ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Zainul Abdin Farroque is the member of parliament for Noakhali-2 (Senbagh upazila and four unions of Sonaimuri upazila) in the 13th Parliament. Elected from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), this freedom fighter has come to Parliament for the sixth time. In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on privileges.

Zainul Abdin Farroque was born on 10 December 1949 in Noakhali district. He is the son of Abdul Haque and Hafeza Khatun. In 1971 he took part in the Liberation War.

Long active in BNP politics, Farroque was elected a member of parliament from Noakhali in the 5th parliamentary election in 1991, the 6th in February 1996, the 7th in June 1996, the 8th in 2001 and the 9th in 2008. In the 9th Parliament, in 2009, he was made Chief Whip of the opposition. He has also served as an adviser to BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the sixth time, winning 83,982 votes in Noakhali-2 with the sheaf of paddy symbol. His late wife, Kaniz Fatema, was also involved in BNP politics. The couple have a daughter.
জয়নুল আবেদীন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে বরিশ:
Zainul Abedin is the member of parliament (MP) for Barishal-3 (Muladi and Babuganj) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). On 13 July 2026 he was appointed chair of the standing committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs. He is also a member of the special committee on amending the Constitution. In the party he is a vice-chairman of the BNP.

Zainul Abedin was born on 27 July 1953 in the village of Purba Hosnabad in Muladi upazila, Barishal district. He is the son of Dalil Uddin and Amena Begum. After passing the SSC from A.K. School in Barishal in 1967 and the HSC in 1969, he obtained from the University of Dhaka a bachelor's degree (Honours) in political science in 1974, a master's degree in 1975 and an LLB degree in 1977. In the Liberation War of 1971 he took part in Sector 9.

He entered the legal profession in 1980 on being enrolled as an advocate. He was enrolled as an advocate of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in 1984 and of the Appellate Division in the mid-1990s. In 2003 he was given the status of senior advocate. As a leader of the profession, he was elected assistant secretary of the Supreme Court Bar Association in 1991, its general secretary in 1997 and its president in 2012, 2017 and 2018. He was elected a member of the Bangladesh Bar Council in 2005 and 2022, and serves as vice-chairman of the Bar Council.

Involved in student politics since 1966, Zainul Abedin was elected central president of Bangla Chhatra League in 1974. In late 1978 he became involved in the politics of President Ziaur Rahman, and in 1979 he was appointed director of the Institute of Political Education founded by Ziaur Rahman. In 1991 he became a founding member of Jatiyatabadi Ainjibi Forum (the Nationalist Lawyers' Forum). In 2001 he was convener of the legal cell of the BNP's central election steering committee. He later served as the party's central legal affairs secretary and as adviser to the chairperson.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Barishal-3 with 80,930 votes on the sheaf of paddy symbol. Alongside his legal practice, he is involved in helping poor students, developing local educational and health institutions, and disaster relief and rehabilitation work.
জহির উদ্দিন স্বপন মন্ত্রীর পদমর্যাদায় প:
Zahir Uddin Swapon is Political Adviser to the Prime Minister, with the rank of a minister, and the member of parliament (MP) for Barishal-1 (Gouranadi-Agailjhara). He was sworn in as Minister of Information and Broadcasting on 17 February 2026, and has been Adviser to the Prime Minister since 21 August. The founding convener of the BNP media cell, Swapon was for a long time one of the party's spokespeople and an architect of its communication strategy.

He was born on 29 June 1960 in the village of Sarikal in Gouranadi upazila, Barishal; his father is A.K. Mohiuddin. He passed his secondary examination from St Joseph's High School in Khulna in 1975; he was VP of the Government Brajalal College students' union, and later took a master's degree in political science at the University of Dhaka. As a student he was involved in left-wing politics, became central president of Bangladesh Chhatra Moitree and was at the forefront of the anti-autocracy movement.

After joining the BNP in 1993 he quickly became an important member of the party thanks to his skill in media and communication. He led the founding of the party's media cell, and was chief editor of the communication cell and director of Bangladesh Nationalist Research and Communication (BNRC). He became a member of Khaleda Zia's advisory committee; included in the party's advisory council in 2024, he was involved in planning the 2026 election campaign.

He was elected MP for Barishal-1 in the February 1996 and 2001 elections. As an MP he twice represented Bangladesh at the United Nations General Assembly, and was vice-president for the Asia region of Parliamentarians for Global Action, an international network of legislators. In the 2026 election he was elected an MP for the third time with 100,552 votes, by a margin of more than 54,000 votes.
জাকারিয়া তাহের সুমন গৃহায়ন ও গণপূর্ত ম:
Zakaria Taher Sumon is the Minister for Housing and Public Works and the member of parliament for Cumilla-8 (Barura). He took office as minister on 17 February 2026. A businessman, Sumon was previously the member of parliament for Cumilla-7.

He was born in Barura, Cumilla. His father, A. K. M. Abu Taher, was an industrialist, the member of parliament for Cumilla-7, and the founder and chairman of National Bank Limited, the country's first private bank.

When his father's death on 23 September 2004 led to a by-election in Cumilla-7, he won it as the BNP candidate in December that year and came to Parliament for the first time. Elected from Cumilla-8 in the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament, he became a member of parliament for the second time and joined Tarique Rahman's Cabinet.
জি, এম, নজরুল ইসলাম ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদ:
G. M. Nazrul Islam is the member of parliament (MP) for Satkhira-4 (Shyamnagar) in the 13th Parliament. Also known as Gazi Nazrul Islam, this politician has become an MP for the third time.

He was born in 1951 in the village of Ismailpur in Shyamnagar upazila, Satkhira district. He is the son of Janab Ali Gazi and Kanchan Bibi.

In his long political career he served as amir of Shyamnagar upazila Jamaat-e-Islami and as a member of the Satkhira district working council. In the elections to the 5th Parliament in 1991 and the 8th Parliament in 2001, he was elected MP for the then Satkhira-5 seat as the candidate of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. He was also a candidate for Satkhira-4 in the 2008 and 2018 elections.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Satkhira-4 with 106,913 votes on the scales symbol as the nominee of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami.
জীবা আমিনা খান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংর:
Zeeba Amina Khan is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-12 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is a member of the BNP national executive committee and a vice-president of the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal. In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs.

Zeeba Amina Khan was born on 21 June 1962 in Jhalakathi Sadar upazila. She is the daughter of Akhtar Uddin Ahmed and Atia Ahmed. She is a businesswoman by profession.

She is active in the politics of Jhalakathi district. In the election to the 11th Parliament in 2018 she contested Jhalakathi-2 (Sadar and Nalchity) on the BNP's nomination with the sheaf of paddy symbol. In April 2026 the BNP nominated her for a reserved women's seat. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-12 through the votes of the members of parliament.
জোনায়েদ আব্দুর রহিম সাকি পরিকল্পনা প্রত:
Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki is the State Minister for Planning and the member of parliament for Brahmanbaria-6. He has held this post since 4 March 2026. A founding leader and the chief coordinator of Ganosamhati Andolan, Saki has been involved for more than three decades in movements of students and workers, for the protection of national resources, and for democracy and state reform.

He was born on 9 December 1973 in Charlahonia village, Bancharampur upazila, Brahmanbaria; he is the son of Md. Fazlur Rahman and Masuda Khanam. In 1991 he was admitted to the Department of Statistics at the University of Dhaka.

He entered politics through the 1990 mass movement against autocracy and joined the Bangladesh Chhatra Federation. Elected the organisation's central president in 1998, he led various student movements, including those at the University of Dhaka against increases in tuition fees (1998) and against sexual harassment (1999). He left student politics in 2000.

On 29 August 2002 he led the founding of Ganosamhati Andolan together with activists from labour and social movements, and in 2016 he formally became the party's chief coordinator. He had a leading role in the National Committee to Protect Oil, Gas, Mineral Resources, Power and Ports, and directly led the Fulbari movement of 26 August 2006. He played a part in forming several alliances of left parties and, most recently, Ganatantra Mancha. Elected a member of parliament for the first time from Brahmanbaria-6 in the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament, he joined the government.
ড, খন্দকার মোশাররফ হোসেন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয়:
Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain is the member of parliament for Cumilla-1 in the 13th Parliament. A member of the standing committee of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), he has come to Parliament for the fifth time. In 2026 he presided over the first session of the 13th Parliament. In the current Parliament he is a member of the Business Advisory Committee. He is a freedom fighter.

Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain was born on 1 October 1946 in Goyeshpur village, Daudkandi upazila, Cumilla district. He is the son of Khandaker Ashraf Ali and Hosne Ara Hasna Hena. After passing the SSC from Daudkandi High School in 1962, he obtained an MSc degree from the University of Dhaka in 1968. He later pursued higher studies at Imperial College London and obtained a PhD in geology from the University of London in 1973. In 1971 he organised Bangladeshis living in the United Kingdom to build world opinion in support of the Liberation War, and led them as convener of the Chhatra Sangram Parishad (students' action council).

In his career he joined the Department of Geology at the University of Dhaka as a junior lecturer in 1967 and rose in stages to professor. From 1987 to 1990 he was chairman of the department. "Hussain's Method of Extension", which he devised for the structural analysis of geology, has received international recognition. He is a fellow of the Third World Academy of Sciences. He has published 21 research papers in scientific journals at home and abroad. Several of his books have been published, including Muktijuddhe Bilat Probashider Obodan ("The contribution of Bangladeshis in Britain to the Liberation War"), Amar Rajnitir Rojnamcha ("My political diary") and Sangsade Kotha Bola Jay ("One can speak in Parliament").

In 1979 he joined BNP at the call of President Ziaur Rahman. After serving as the party's student affairs secretary, joint secretary general and president of Cumilla (North) district BNP, he has been a member of the party's standing committee since 1994. He was elected a member of parliament from Cumilla four times. From 1991 to 1996 he was Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, and in 1996 he briefly served as Home Minister. From 2001 to 2006 he was Minister for Health and Family Welfare. In 2002 he became president of the 56th World Health Assembly, and he received the World Health Organization's World No Tobacco award for his contribution to the anti-tobacco campaign in the country.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament, winning 141,440 votes in Cumilla-1 with the sheaf of paddy symbol. He set up the Dr Mosharraf Foundation for education, employment and healthcare in the area. With its funding, several colleges, schools, orphanages and madrasas have been established in Daudkandi, Eliotganj, Gouripur and Titas.
ড. আ ন ম এহছানুল হক মিলন শিক্ষামন্ত্রী এ:
Dr A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milon is the Minister for Education and Minister for Primary and Mass Education, and the member of parliament for Chandpur-1. He took charge of the two ministries on 17 February 2026. As State Minister for Education in the 2001–2006 term, he became known across the country for his drive against cheating in public examinations. A writer and educationist, Milon is international affairs secretary of BNP's central executive committee.

He was born in Kachua, Chandpur; he is the son of Obaidul Haque and Mahmuda Khatun. He passed the SSC from Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Government Boys' High School in Dhaka and the HSC from Government Intermediate Technical College (now Government Science College). After a bachelor's degree in chemistry from the University of Dhaka, he went to the United States in 1982 and completed an MBA at the New York Institute of Technology. In 2018 he received a PhD in political science from the International Islamic University Malaysia; his research was on the role of technical and vocational education in the socio-economic development of Bangladesh.

Although involved in politics since his student days, he became active in national politics in the mid-1990s. He was first elected a member of parliament from Chandpur-1 in the 7th parliamentary election in 1996. In 2001 he won again, defeating the Awami League candidate, former minister Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, by a large margin, and became State Minister for Education. His zero-tolerance policy against cheating at examination centres is regarded as a milestone in restoring discipline to public examinations.

After a long gap, elected a member of parliament for the third time from the same seat in 2026, he was given charge of the country's entire education sector, from schools to universities.
ড. আবদুল মঈন খান স্থানীয় সরকার, পল্লী উ:
Dr. Abdul Moyeen Khan is Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives and MP for Narsingdi-2. He was sworn in as minister on 21 August 2026. An academic turned politician, he has been elected MP five times.

He was born on 1 January 1947 in Palash, Narsingdi. His father, Abdul Momen Khan, was the country's Cabinet Secretary, a founding member of the BNP and Food Minister in President Ziaur Rahman's cabinet; his mother is Khorsheda Begum. After completing his higher secondary education at Notre Dame College, Dhaka, he obtained a PhD from the University of Sussex in the United Kingdom in 1973.

Before entering politics he was a professor of physics at the University of Dhaka. He was first elected MP from Narsingdi-2 in the election to the 5th Parliament in 1991, and won the same seat again in 1996 and 2001. In Khaleda Zia's third cabinet he was Minister for Science and Information and Communication Technology. In 1998 he became a member of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Planning.

Although defeated in the 2008 and 2018 elections, he remained active in the party's central politics; in December 2009 he became a member of the standing committee, the BNP's highest policy-making forum. He was always at the forefront of the party's contacts with foreign diplomats. In the 13th parliamentary election he was elected again from Narsingdi-2.
ড. খলিলুর রহমান বাংলাদেশের পররাষ্ট্রমন্ত:
Dr. Khalilur Rahman is Bangladesh's Minister of Foreign Affairs and President of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. He became Foreign Minister under the technocrat quota on 17 February 2026; he is not a member of parliament. He was elected President of the General Assembly on 2 June 2026 and took office on 8 September. He is the second Bangladeshi to hold this post, after Humayun Rasheed Choudhury in 1986-87.

He was born on 1 April 1954 in Nawabganj upazila, Dhaka. After completing his higher secondary education at Dhaka Residential Model College, he obtained a master's degree in economics from the University of Dhaka, coming first in the first class. He also came first in the 1977 BCS examination. He later obtained a master's degree in law and diplomacy from The Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts University in the United States and a PhD in economics from the Kennedy School at Harvard University.

Joining the civil service in 1979, he worked in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and as private secretary to the Foreign Minister. While at Bangladesh's Permanent Mission to the United Nations, he represented Bangladesh on the General Assembly's Economic and Financial Committee and was spokesperson for the least developed countries. He then served as head of the New York office of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) and as a special adviser in Geneva, and was responsible for economic, social and development matters in the Executive Office of the UN Secretary-General. He played a part in drawing up the programme for the least developed countries at the 2001 Brussels conference, which included provisions for duty-free and quota-free market access for their goods. In 2012 he became head of the policy development and coordination branch of the Office of the UN High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States.

In 2001 he was for a short time private secretary to Justice Latifur Rahman, Chief Adviser of the caretaker government. After the July mass uprising, on 19 November 2024 he was appointed the Chief Adviser's High Representative on the Rohingya crisis and priority issues, and from April 2025 he also served as National Security Adviser. He is one of the founders of East West University and a member of its board of trustees.
ড. নিলোফার চৌধুরী মনি ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সং:
Dr Nilufar Chowdhury Moni is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-10 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Nilufar Chowdhury Moni was born on 15 August 1969 in Pathalia village, Jamalpur district. She is the daughter of Nazrul Islam Chowdhury and Kohinoor Chowdhury.

She obtained a master's degree in political science from the University of Dhaka in 1995 and an LLB from the same university in 1998. In 2011 she obtained a PhD for research on women's empowerment. She is a lawyer by profession.

Nilufar Chowdhury Moni is an assistant secretary of the BNP central committee and chief coordinator of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Torun Projonmo Dal (Bangladesh Nationalist Young Generation Party). In 2009 she was a BNP-nominated member of parliament for women's seat 37 in the 9th Parliament. Her name was on the BNP's announced list for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament as a former member of parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-10 through the votes of the members of parliament. She is the mother of two children.
ড. মুহাম্মদ ওসমান ফারুক ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয়:
Dr. Muhammad Osman Farruk is the member of parliament for Kishoreganj-3 (Tarail and Karimganj Upazilas) in the 13th Parliament. Elected for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), this academic and politician has entered Parliament for the second time. He previously served as Bangladesh's Minister of Education.

Osman Farruk was born on 18 July 1940. His ancestral home is in Boiratiapara village, Gujadia Union, Karimganj Upazila, Kishoreganj District. His father, Dr. Muhammad Osman Ghani, was a renowned educationist and former member of parliament who served as vice-chancellor of the University of Dhaka and of Bangladesh Agricultural University. His mother is Shamsunnahar Ghani.

He passed his matriculation from St. Gregory's School in 1956 and his intermediate examination from Dhaka College in 1958. He obtained a bachelor's degree with honours in economics in 1961 and a master's degree in 1962 from the University of Dhaka. After joining a USAID fellowship programme in 1963, he earned an MS in agricultural economics from the University of Texas in the United States in 1964 and a doctorate in agricultural economics from Cornell University in 1970. The same year he joined Bangladesh Agricultural University as an associate professor, where he taught operations and marketing.

He joined the BNP in 2001 and the same year was elected member of parliament for Kishoreganj-4 in the election to the 8th Parliament. He was appointed Minister of Education in Begum Khaleda Zia's cabinet. He has also served as an adviser to the BNP Chairperson, Khaleda Zia.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as the BNP candidate for Kishoreganj-3 with 112,466 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.
ড. রাশেদ আল মাহমুদ তিতুমীর মন্ত্রীর পদমর:
Dr. Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir is Adviser to the Prime Minister with the rank of a Minister; since 24 February 2026 he has been responsible for the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Planning. An economist, Titumir is a professor at the University of Dhaka and a former chairman of its Department of Development Studies; his research on development economics, poverty, climate change and political economy has been published internationally. He is not a member of parliament.

He was born in Machhpara village, Pangsha, Rajbari; his father, Arshed Ali, is a former principal of Pangsha College. After completing his SSC and HSC at Jhenaidah Cadet College, he obtained a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Dhaka in 1990. He obtained a master's degree in development and financial economics from the University of London in 1997, a postgraduate diploma in trade policy and commercial diplomacy from Carleton University and the University of Ottawa in Canada in 2005, and a PhD in economics from the University of London in 2014.

In the Department of Development Studies at the University of Dhaka he was assistant professor, associate professor and later full professor, and as chairman of the department he introduced an outcome-based curriculum. He was an assistant professor at Bangladesh Open University and a teaching and research fellow at Royal Holloway, London. He has worked as a member of the Ministry of Commerce's WTO advisory committee, a member of the Bangladesh delegation to the UN climate conference and a national consultant to the Bangladesh Tariff Commission; he has been a consultant to the ILO, UNDP, UNESCAP, DFID and the European Union.

He is the founding chairman of the research organisation 'Unnayan Onneshan', vice-chair of the Asia Regional Committee of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and chairman of its Bangladesh National Committee. His books include Why Agriculture Productivity Falls (Purdue University Press), State Building and Social Policies in Developing Countries (Routledge), Numbers and Narratives in Bangladesh's Economic Development and Sundarbans and its Ecosystem Services (Palgrave Macmillan). He writes columns regularly; he was at one time a staff reporter at The Daily Star. He has received various fellowships, including a Charles Wallace Trust scholarship.
ডাঃ মোঃ আনোয়ারুল হক ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংস:
Dr. Md. Anwarul Haque is the member of parliament for Netrokona-2 (Netrokona Sadar and Barhatta Upazilas) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He is president of Netrokona District BNP.

Anwarul Haque was born on 1 April 1967 in Netrokona Sadar Upazila, Netrokona District. He is the son of Md. Abdul Hamid and Nurjahan Begum. He is a physician by profession.

In party politics he served as convener of the Netrokona District BNP convening committee. In August 2025, at the district BNP conference held after a gap of eleven years, he was elected president of the district BNP with 1,275 votes cast by councillors.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as the BNP's nominated candidate with 171,399 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.
ডাঃ মোঃ মাহাবুবুর রহমান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয়:
Dr. Md. Mahbubur Rahman is the member of parliament for Mymensingh-7 (Trishal Upazila) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). A physician and politician, Mahbubur Rahman is better known as Dr. Liton. In Parliament he is a member of the Standing Committee on Public Accounts and of the Library Committee, and also serves as chair of Sub-committee No. 3 of the Library Committee.

He was born on 21 October 1963 in Singrail village, Trishal Upazila, Mymensingh. His father, Md. Habibur Rahman, was an agriculturist and his mother, Farida Akter, a teacher. After passing the SSC from St. Joseph High School in Dhaka and the HSC from Notre Dame College, he obtained an MBBS degree from Dhaka Medical College. He later went to the United Kingdom for higher studies and earned an MSc from the University of London.

Professionally, Dr. Liton is one of the directors of the Labaid Group and is associated with State University of Bangladesh. He was a member of the syndicate of Jatiya Kabi Kazi Nazrul Islam University and has served as chair of the governing bodies of Nazrul Degree College and Trishal Mohila Degree College.

He has been involved in politics since his student days. He was president of the Dhaka Medical College unit of Chhatra Dal and a member of the central council of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal. In professional politics he was the founding member secretary of the Doctors Association of Bangladesh (DAB). After the BNP formed the government in 1991, he served as assistant private secretary to the then Health Minister, Chowdhury Kamal Ibne Yusuf. He has also served as a member of the BNP Central Executive Committee and as convener of Mymensingh South District BNP.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as the BNP's nominated candidate with 99,049 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol, and took the oath as a member of parliament on 17 February.
ডাঃ মোঃ শফিকুর রহমান ঢাকা-১৫ আসন থেকে নি:
Dr Md Shafiqur Rahman is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Dhaka-15 and Leader of the Opposition in Parliament. He is the ameer of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. This is his first term in Parliament. In Parliament he is a member of the Business Advisory Committee and the Standing Committee on Privileges.

Shafiqur Rahman was born on 31 October 1958 in Bhatera Union, Kulaura Upazila, Moulvibazar District. His father is Md. Abru Mia. He is the third of four siblings.

He passed his SSC in 1974 from the local Baramchal High School and his HSC in 1976 from Murarichand (MC) College, Sylhet. In 1983 he obtained his MBBS degree from Sylhet Medical College. He is a physician by profession.

In 1977 he joined Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir and served as president of its Sylhet Medical College branch and later of its Sylhet branch. He joined Jamaat-e-Islami in 1984 and served as its ameer for Sylhet. He took on the posts of central assistant secretary general in 2010, acting secretary general in 2011 and secretary general in 2016. On 12 November 2019 he was elected ameer of the party, and he was re-elected ameer for a third term, for the 2025–2028 term.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Dhaka-15 with 85,131 votes under the scales symbol.

Alongside politics, he has been involved in founding and running various service institutions, notably Sylhet Women's Medical College. In 1985 he married Amena Begum, who was a member of the 8th Parliament in a reserved seat. The couple have two daughters and a son.
ডা. আবু মনসুর সাখাওয়াত হাসান হবিগঞ্জ-২:
Dr Abu Mansur Sakhawat Hassan is the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) member of parliament elected from Habiganj-2. A physician and politician, Sakhawat Hassan is serving in Parliament for the first time, as a member of the 13th Parliament.

He was born on 5 December 1956 in Kamalkhani village, Baniachong upazila, Habiganj district. He is the son of Toyobul Hasan and Foyezunnesa Hasan. By profession he is a physician.

He has long been involved in BNP politics. Within the party he served as organising secretary for Sylhet division and later became a member of the BNP chairperson's advisory council. He also contested the 2008 parliamentary election.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the first time, winning 126,583 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol. He is married to Rabeya Sultana and is the father of two sons and a daughter.
ডা. ইকরামুল বারী টিপু ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সং:
Dr Ekramul Bari Tipu is the member of parliament (MP) in the 13th Parliament for Naogaon-4, a seat made up of Manda upazila. A physician by profession, he entered Parliament for the first time as the candidate nominated by the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party).

He was born on 1 March 1965 in Manda upazila of Naogaon district. His father's name is Mofiz Uddin Mollah and his mother's name is Khatejan Bewa.

He completed his MBBS degree at Rajshahi Medical College, under the University of Rajshahi, and obtained a postgraduate degree from Dhaka Shishu (Children's) Hospital.

In politics, Ekramul Bari Tipu has served as chairman of the Manda upazila parishad. Before the election he was a member of the Manda upazila BNP. He was one of the twelve physicians the BNP nominated for the 13th parliamentary election. In the election on 12 February 2026 he was elected with 133,928 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol. The Jamaat-e-Islami candidate for the seat, Md. Abdur Rakib, received 97,585 votes.
ডা. এ জেড এম জাহিদ হোসেন মহিলা ও শিশু বি:
Dr A Z M Zahid Hossain is the Minister for Women and Children Affairs and for Social Welfare, and the member of parliament for Dinajpur-6. He was sworn in as minister of the two ministries on 17 February 2026. A well-known urologist, he is a member of the BNP's national standing committee and was for a long time Khaleda Zia's personal physician. He has been elected to Parliament for the first time, in the 13th Parliament.

He was born on 25 December 1960 in Gafargaon, Mymensingh; his ancestral home is in the village of Motihara in Putimara union of Nawabganj upazila, Dinajpur. He took his MBBS from Mymensingh Medical College in 1983. He then obtained an FCPS from the Bangladesh College of Physicians and Surgeons (1997), an MS in urology from the University of Dhaka (2001), an FCPS from the College of Physicians and Surgeons Pakistan (2004) and an FRCP fellowship from the Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh in the United Kingdom (2006). He was a professor of urology at Bangladesh Medical University.

He joined Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal politics while studying at Mymensingh Medical College. He has been involved with the Doctors Association of Bangladesh (DAB) since 1989, and was its secretary general for four terms between 1998 and 2019. He was general secretary of the Bangladesh Medical Association, and became member secretary of the Bangladesh Sammilito Peshajibi Parishad in 2005 and its convener in 2022.

He became a member of the BNP Chairperson's advisory council in 2010, a vice-chairman of the party at its 2016 council, and a member of the national standing committee on 16 August 2024. He has been imprisoned three times for political reasons: in 2009, 2011 and 2013.
ডা. এস,এম, রফিকুল ইসলাম, যিনি রফিকুল ইসল:
Dr S.M. Rafiqul Islam, known as Rafiqul Islam Bachchu, is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Gazipur-3 (Sreepur Upazila and part of Gazipur Sadar). This is his first term in Parliament, as the nominee of the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party). In September 2026 he was nominated chair of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

He was born on 12 May 1963 in Sreepur, Gazipur District. His father is Shamsuddin Ahmed and his mother Razia Khatun. He is a physician by profession and has long been involved in politics alongside his medical practice.

Rafiqul Islam is assistant health affairs secretary of the BNP's central executive committee and first joint convener of the Gazipur District BNP.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Gazipur-3 with 162,343 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol. With this victory a BNP candidate won the seat after a long gap of 47 years.
ডা. কে এম বাবর গোপালগঞ্জ-২ (গোপালগঞ্জ সদ:
Dr K M Babor is a Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) member of parliament elected from Gopalganj-2 (Gopalganj Sadar and part of Kashiani). This is his first term, in the 13th Parliament. Locally he is also known as ‘Dr Babor, the doctor of the poor’.

K M Babor was born on 25 January 1982 in Gopinathpur village, Majhigati Union, Gopalganj Sadar Upazila. His father is Md. Surat Ali Khan and his mother Momejan Begum. He is a physician by profession.

Having risen in politics from the grassroots, this physician received the BNP nomination and stood as a candidate for Gopalganj-2. In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for the first time, with 40,048 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.

In his personal life he is the father of a son and a daughter. His wife, Dr Rabeya Akter, is also a physician by profession.
ডা. জাহেদ উর রহমান প্রতিমন্ত্রীর পদমর্যা:
Dr. Zahed Ur Rahman is Adviser on policy and strategy to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, with the rank of a State Minister; he was appointed on 17 February 2026, and since 12 March he has also been responsible for the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. A physician by profession, Zahed Ur Rahman is known as a columnist and political analyst; he was a member of the interim government's Electoral System Reform Commission. He is not a member of parliament.

His ancestral home is in Kotra Mohabbatpur village, Gopalpur union, Begumganj upazila, Noakhali. Because of his father's job, he spent much of his childhood at Chandraghona in Kaptai, on the bank of the Karnaphuli river. He passed his secondary examination from Karnaphuli Paper Mills High School in 1991 and his higher secondary examination from Government Hazi Muhammad Mohsin College in Chattogram. He obtained an MBBS from Dhaka Medical College and an MBA from the Institute of Business Administration (IBA), University of Dhaka.

Alongside his medical profession he has taught at various educational institutions. He writes columns regularly in print and online media; democracy, elections, political violence, enforced disappearances and human rights are the main subjects of his writing and analysis. In 2025-26 his analyses of elections and political consensus in Prothom Alo drew attention. He takes part in discussions on various media, including Deutsche Welle and Jamuna Television, and publishes regular videos on contemporary politics on his YouTube and Facebook channel 'Zahed's Take'. He is the author of the book 'Janapriyatama Lekhaker Mrityu Bikrir Galpa' (The story of selling the death of the most popular writer).
ডা. মোঃ আব্দুল বারী সরদার ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয:
Dr Md. Abdul Bari Sarder is the member of parliament (MP) in the 13th Parliament for Rajshahi-4, a seat made up of Bagmara upazila. He entered Parliament for the first time as the candidate of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. He is the first Jamaat-e-Islami MP from this seat since independence. In the party he serves as nayeb-e-amir (deputy amir) of Bagmara upazila.

He was born on 9 February 1970 in Bagmara upazila of Rajshahi district. His father's name is Mohammad Ali and his mother's name is Mst. Khoshmon Bewa.

A physician with an MBBS degree from Rajshahi Medical College, he chose not to take up a salaried job but to stay in his home area and provide medical care at low cost. He has been treating the people of Bagmara for about 30 years and has become known locally as the ‘humane doctor’. He founded the Bhabaniganj Clinic.

In the 13th parliamentary election on 12 February 2026 he was elected with 115,226 votes under the scales symbol. The BNP candidate for the seat, D. M. D. Ziaur Rahman, received 109,461 votes.

He has not given up medical practice since taking the oath as an MP. In line with his election manifesto, he sees patients free of charge at his own clinic every Friday. In his words, ‘If the people of Bagmara are well, that is my greatest reward.’
ডা. সানসিলা জেবরিন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Dr Sunsila Jabrin is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-15 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is a joint convener of the Sherpur district BNP.

Sunsila Jabrin Priyanka was born on 22 June 1993 in Sherpur district. Her father, Dr Md. Hazrat Ali, is general secretary of the Sherpur district BNP. Her mother is Nilufa Khanam.

She passed the SSC in 2008 and the HSC in 2010 from Agrani School and College in Dhaka. In 2016 she obtained an MBBS degree from Anwer Khan Modern Medical College. A physician by profession, Priyanka has worked as an honorary medical officer at Dhaka Medical College and served as a lecturer in the microbiology department of Anwer Khan Modern Medical College in Dhanmondi. She is a member of the Doctors Association of Bangladesh.

In the election to the 11th Parliament in 2018 she contested Sherpur-1 as the BNP candidate, becoming the youngest candidate in the country. In the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament she was again the BNP candidate for Sherpur-1. On 20 April 2026 the BNP nominated her for a reserved women's seat. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-15 through the votes of the members of parliament and took the oath on 5 May 2026.
তারেক রহমান বাংলাদেশের প্রধানমন্ত্রী, সং:
Tarique Rahman is Prime Minister of Bangladesh, Leader of the House and chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). He was sworn in as Prime Minister on 17 February 2026. He is the eldest son of former President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, and is also known as Tarique Zia.

He was born in Dhaka on 20 November 1968; his ancestral home is in Gabtali, Bogura. After his SSC at Dhaka Residential Model College and his higher secondary education at Adamjee Cantonment College, he was admitted to the University of Dhaka in the 1985–86 academic session, first in the Department of Law and later in the Department of International Relations. He left his studies in the second year of his undergraduate course and went into business in the textile and shipping sectors.

His political career began in 1988 as a primary member of the Gabtali Upazila BNP. He was active in the party's campaign across the country in the 1991 and 2001 elections. In 2002 he became senior joint secretary general of the BNP, and on 8 December 2009 he was elected senior vice-chairman at the party's fifth national council. He later served as the party's acting chairman from London.

He was arrested in 2007 under the army-backed caretaker government and, after his release in September 2008 following about eighteen months, went to London for medical treatment. Between 2007 and 2024, 84 cases were filed against him, in some of which he was convicted; the BNP had consistently called them politically motivated. After the July 2024 mass uprising, the courts acquitted him in all the cases and set aside the sentences.

After nearly seventeen years abroad, he returned home on 25 December 2025 with his wife Zubaida Rahman and daughter Zaima Rahman. He became the party's chairman on 9 January 2026. In that year's parliamentary election the BNP under his leadership won two-thirds of the seats; he himself won both seats, Dhaka-17 and Bogura-6, and later gave up the Bogura seat. As Prime Minister he has also kept charge of the Cabinet Division and of the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces Division. In April 2026 Time magazine included him in its list of the world's 100 most influential people.
তাসমিয়া প্রধান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সং:
Tasmia Prodhan is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-47 in the 13th Parliament. She is president of the Jatiya Ganatantrik Party (JAGPA) and entered Parliament as a nominee of the 11-party electoral alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami. In Parliament she is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs.

Barrister Tasmia Prodhan was born at her maternal grandparents' home in Bogura. Her paternal home is in Tokrabhasha village, Chilahati union, Debiganj upazila, Panchagarh district. She is the daughter of Shafiul Alam Prodhan, the founding president of JAGPA. Her mother, Rehana Prodhan, taught sociology at Lalmatia Mohila College and was JAGPA's second president. Gomir Uddin Prodhan, Speaker of the East Pakistan Provincial Assembly, was her paternal grandfather.

She passed her secondary examination from Mohammadpur Preparatory School and College in 1996 and her higher secondary examination from Viqarunnisa Noon School and College in 1998. In 2004 she completed a bachelor's degree in law at the University of London, obtained the Bar-at-Law from Lincoln's Inn, and returned home in 2007. After returning she worked at Dr. Hamid and Associates and at Moudud Ahmed and Associates. In 2010 she began practising as a lawyer in the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and founded her own law chamber, Tasmia Prodhan and Associates.

In politics she was vice-president of JAGPA. In October 2018 she was made acting president of the party, and on 9 November of the same year she was elected president at the party council. In 2018 she stood as a candidate for Panchagarh-2 in the election to the 11th Parliament.

In 2026 the 11-party electoral alliance nominated her for a reserved seat for women. As the only candidate for this seat, which is filled by a vote of members of parliament, she was elected unopposed, and the Election Commission published the gazette on 30 April 2026. In her personal life she is the mother of three daughters.
দীপেন দেওয়ান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে পার্:
Dipen Dewan is the member of parliament for the hill district seat of Rangamati in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). When the new cabinet led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was formed on 17 February 2026, he was sworn in as Minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs, and he held this office until 1 June.

Dipen Dewan was born into a political family on 8 June 1963 in Rangamati hill district. His father, the late Subimal Dewan, was adviser on tribal affairs to President Ziaur Rahman and a founding leader of the Rangamati district BNP. His mother, the late Mohini Dewan, was a homemaker. He belongs to the Chakma community.

After passing the SSC in 1978 he completed his higher secondary education at Rangamati Government College. While studying there he was one of the founding organisers of the college unit of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal. He later obtained LLB and LLM degrees from the Department of Law of the University of Dhaka. He joined the 7th BCS (Judicial) cadre and served as a judge for 19 years.

In 2005 he resigned from the post of joint district judge and joined the BNP. In 2010 he became president of the Rangamati district BNP, and since 2016 he has served as joint secretary for religious affairs on the party's central committee. He is a member of the BNP national executive committee.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected for the Rangamati seat, winning 201,544 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol. His margin over the nearest candidate was 170,322 votes, the largest margin in the country in this election. He is married to Moitri Chakma and is the father of two daughters, Aditi and Rajeshwari Dewan.
দেওয়ান মোহাম্মদ সালাউদ্দিন ঢাকা-১৯ আসন:
Dewan Mohammod Salahuddin is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Dhaka-19. This BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) leader has become an MP for the third time. He was previously elected in 1996 and 2001 from what was then Dhaka-12.

He was born on 1 October 1962 in Jirabo village, Yearpur Union, Savar Upazila, Dhaka. His father is Dewan Md. Idris and his mother Saleha Idris; he is the second of six children. He entered Momenshahi Cadet College in 1974 and passed his SSC in 1978 and his HSC in 1980. In 1987 he obtained his MBBS degree from Mymensingh Medical College.

In 1991, having passed the 10th BCS (Health) examination, he joined Itna Upazila Health Complex in Kishoreganj as a medical officer, and in 1993 he was transferred to Savar Upazila Health Complex. On 1 January 1996 he voluntarily left government service. A physician, Salahuddin is also known as a writer; he has written about 15 books on various subjects, notable among them Smritite America, Ek Jibone Ami and Rajnitir Mathe Ghate.

He entered politics in 1990 and became president of the Yearpur Union BNP and, in 2011, of the Ashulia Thana BNP. From 2016 to 2022 he served as president of the Dhaka District BNP. While a member of the 7th Parliament, he became a member of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Health in January 2000.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Dhaka-19 with 190,976 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.

His initiatives to spread education are notable. In 1993 he founded Saleha Idris Primary School, named after his mother, in Srikhandia village, Ashulia; it later became a government school. He founded Jirabo Dewan Idris College in 1996, Dewan Idris Law College in Savar in 2003 and Nischintapur Dewan Idris High School in 2006. In 1992 he married Sabina Siddika Rita; the couple have two children.
নজরুল ইসলাম খান মন্ত্রীর পদমর্যাদায় প্র:
Nazrul Islam Khan is Political Adviser to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, with the rank of a Minister; since 4 March 2026 he has also been responsible for the Ministry of Agriculture. He is a member of the national standing committee, the highest policy-making forum of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party. He is not a member of parliament; he is in the government as an adviser.

He was born in Kulkandi village, Islampur thana, Jamalpur district.

In the 1970s he was an active worker in the labour movement. In 1970 he was president of the workers' union of the then Pakistan Machine Tools Factory (now Bangladesh Machine Tools Factory). On the eve of the Liberation War, when an all-party Mukti Sangram Parishad (liberation struggle council) was formed in Joydebpur, Gazipur, in March 1971, he was its treasurer.

He was chairman of the BNP's election management committee for the 2018 election to the 11th Parliament and the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament.
নাদিয়া পাঠান পাপন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Nadia Pathan Papon is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-32 in the 13th Parliament. Nominated by the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party), she is a member of the party's Dhaka Metropolitan South unit.

Nadia Pathan Papon was born on 31 July 1984. She is the daughter of Syeda Nakhlu Akter and the late Anwar Hossain of Chandura village, Bijoynagar upazila, Brahmanbaria. Her mother is a former vice-chairman of the Bijoynagar Upazila Parishad and a former member of the Zila Parishad (district council).

She passed her SSC from Daudpur High School and her HSC from Kazi Mohammad Shafiqul Islam College. She later received her higher education at Badrunnesa Government Women's College in Dhaka.

She entered politics in 2000 as a member of the Chandura union Chhatra Dal. While studying at Badrunnesa Government Women's College she served as general secretary of the college Chhatra Dal, and she later also held leadership positions at the central level.

Nadia Pathan Papon was one of the 36 people whose names the BNP announced on 20 April 2026 for the reserved seats for women. As the only candidate for this seat, which is filled by a vote of members of parliament, she was elected unopposed, and the Election Commission published the gazette on 30 April 2026. After being nominated, she pledged to work for the welfare of the disadvantaged women and children of society.
নায়াব ইউসুফ আহমেদ ফরিদপুর-৩ (ফরিদপুর সদ:
Nayab Yusuf Ahmed is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Faridpur-3 (Faridpur Sadar). This is her first term in Parliament, as the nominee of the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party). She is one of the seven women who won by direct vote in the 2026 election. In Parliament she is a member of the House Committee, the Library Committee, and Sub-committees No. 3 and No. 4 of the Library Committee.

Known as Nayab Yusuf, she was born on 3 February 1970. She is a member of the Biswas Estate family of Faridpur. Her father, Chowdhury Kamal Ibne Yusuf (1940–2020), was a vice-chairman of the BNP, a three-time member of parliament and Minister for Food and Disaster Management and Relief. Her mother is Shaila Kamal. Nayab, her parents' elder daughter, has a brother, Chowdhury Saud Yusuf.

In politics she is a member of the BNP's National Executive Committee and assistant organising secretary for Faridpur Division.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, she was elected MP for Faridpur-3 with 148,545 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.
নাসির উদ্দিন আহমেদ মৌলভীবাজার-১ (বড়লেখা:
Nasir Uddin Ahmed is the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) member of parliament elected from Maulvibazar-1 (Barlekha and Juri). Known as Nasir Uddin Ahmed Mithu, this businessman, industrialist and politician is serving in Parliament for the first time, as a member of the 13th Parliament.

He was born in 1965. He is the son of Aftab Uddin Ahmad and Amena Khatun. By profession he is a businessman and industrialist.

In party politics he is a former vice-president of Maulvibazar district BNP and a member of the district BNP's convening committee.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the first time, winning 98,282 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
নাসের রহমান মৌলভীবাজার-৩ (মৌলভীবাজার সদর:
Nasser Rahman is the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) member of parliament elected from Maulvibazar-3 (Moulvibazar Sadar and Rajnagar). Known as M. Nasser Rahman, the politician is serving in Parliament for the second time. In the 13th Parliament he is chair of the standing committee on the Ministry of Land.

Nasser Rahman was born on 29 August 1962. His father, M. Saifur Rahman, was a former finance minister of Bangladesh and a member of parliament. His mother was the late Durre Samad Rahman. By profession he is a businessman.

In the 2001 general election his father won two seats, Sylhet-1 and Maulvibazar-3, and kept Sylhet-1. In the Maulvibazar-3 by-election in November 2001, Nasser Rahman was elected a member of parliament for the first time. He is president of the Saifur Rahman Foundation.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the second time, winning 156,757 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol. He is married to Regina Rahman.
নিতাই রায় চৌধুরী সংস্কৃতি বিষয়ক মন্ত্র:
Nitai Roy Chowdhury is the Minister of Cultural Affairs and the member of parliament (MP) for Magura-2. He was sworn in as minister on 17 February 2026. A lawyer by profession, he is a vice-chairman of the BNP; he has returned to the Cabinet after three and a half decades.

He was born on 7 January 1949 in Hatbaria village of Mohammadpur upazila, Magura; his father is Kalipada Roy Chowdhury. He studied at the University of Dhaka and has been involved in politics since his student days.

In the 4th parliamentary election in 1988 he became MP for Magura-2 on the Jatiya Party's nomination, and served as chairman of the Magura Zila Parishad (district council) with the rank of a minister. He was State Minister for Youth and Sports from 2 May to 9 September 1990, and then Minister of Youth and Sports until 6 December. After the fall of the Ershad government he joined the BNP.

Although he was defeated in Magura-2 in the 1991, 2001, 2008 and 2018 elections, he remained in the party's central leadership. In the 2026 election he was elected MP for the second time. His wife is Jhuma Roy Chowdhury; they have two sons and three daughters, including Nipun Roy Chowdhury.
নিপুন রায় চৌধুরী ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Nipun Roy Chowdhury is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-11 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is general secretary of the Dhaka district BNP and a member of the BNP central executive committee. In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Nipun Roy Chowdhury was born on 29 October 1987. She grew up in a political family. Her father, Advocate Nitai Roy Chowdhury, is a vice-chairman of the BNP, the member of parliament for Magura-2 and Minister for Cultural Affairs. Her mother is Jhumur Roy Chowdhury. Her father-in-law, Goyasawar Chandra Roy, is a member of the BNP's national standing committee and the member of parliament for Dhaka-3.

She is a former student of Eden Mohila College and a lawyer by profession. She has been active in politics since her student days. Alongside her post in the Dhaka district BNP, she serves as president of the South Keraniganj BNP and as secretary of the Women and Children's Rights Forum.

Nipun Roy is one of the 36 people the BNP nominated for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-11 through the votes of the members of parliament. Her brother, Debashish Roy Chowdhury, is a justice of the Supreme Court.
নুরুল আমিন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে চট্টগ্র:
Nurul Amin is the member of parliament for Chattogram-1 (Mirsharai) in the 13th Parliament. Locally he is known as Nurul Amin Chairman. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Nurul Amin was born on 10 January 1968 in Patakot, in Osmanpur union of Mirsharai upazila, Chattogram. He is the son of Abul Khair and Talimer Nesa. He is a businessman by profession.

His career as an elected representative began in local government. In 1998 he was elected a member of the Osmanpur union parishad, and in 2003 chairman of the same union parishad. In 2014 he was elected chairman of the Mirsharai upazila parishad. Within the party he has served as general secretary of the Mirsharai upazila BNP. He also received the BNP nomination in the election to the 11th Parliament in 2018.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-1 as the BNP candidate, winning 128,799 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol. He is married to Nur Nahar and is the father of four sons and three daughters.
নূরুন্নিসা সিদ্দীকা ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদ:
Nurun Nesa Siddiqua is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-37 in the 13th Parliament. Nominated by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, she is secretary of the party's central women's wing and a member of its central executive council. In Parliament she is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Women and Children Affairs.

Known as Principal Nurun Nesa Siddiqua, the educationist was born in 1958 in Char Kakra village, Companiganj upazila, Noakhali district. Her father is Noman Siddiqui and her mother is Hasmatunnesa. She is the youngest of nine brothers and sisters. Her husband, Sheikh Mohammad Mohiuddin, is a retired professor of Tejgaon College.

She studied up to class eight at Peshkarhat High School. She later completed her secondary education at Azimpur Government Girls' School and College in Dhaka and her higher secondary education at Eden Mohila College, and then completed her bachelor's and master's degrees in Bangla. She is a principal by profession.

She is a founding member of Bangladesh Islami Chhatri Sangstha and for a long time served as the organisation's second central president. In 1990 she joined Jamaat's women's wing.

On 20 April 2026, when the 11-party electoral alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami announced 13 names for the reserved seats for women, her name was at the top of the list. As the only candidate for this seat, which is filled by a vote of members of parliament, she was elected unopposed, and the Election Commission published the gazette on 30 April 2026. She has expressed the hope of working in Parliament to protect the rights of women and children.
নূরুল ইসলাম মনি ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে বর:
Nurul Islam Moni is the member of parliament (MP) for Barguna-2 (Pathorghata, Bamna and Betagi) in the 13th Parliament and the Chief Whip of Parliament. A central vice-chairman of the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party), this experienced parliamentarian has been elected an MP for the fourth time. He was appointed Chief Whip on 2 March 2026. He is currently chair of the House Committee and a member of the Business Advisory Committee, the special committee on amending the Constitution, the Standing Committee on Privileges and the standing committee on the Ministry of Finance.

He was born in the village of Monipur in Pathorghata upazila, Barguna district. He is the son of Mazhar Uddin and Ambia Khatun. After passing his higher secondary examination under the Jashore Education Board in 1972, he obtained a BSc from the University of Dhaka in 1975 and an MSc with a first class in 1976.

He was first elected MP for Barguna-2 as an independent candidate in the election to the 4th Parliament in 1988. He won again as an independent candidate in the election to the 5th Parliament in 1991, and later joined the BNP. He was elected president of Barguna district BNP. In the election to the 8th Parliament in 2001 he became an MP for the third time, as the BNP candidate. In the 8th Parliament he was chair of the parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Science and Information and Communication Technology, and also served as a panel speaker.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Barguna-2 for the fourth time with 90,643 votes on the sheaf of paddy symbol. After the election he was given the post of Chief Whip of Parliament.
নেওয়াজ হালিমা আরলী ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদ:
Newaz Halima Arly is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-5 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is assistant relief and rehabilitation secretary of the central BNP. In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges.

Newaz Halima Arly was born on 30 August 1969 in Char Goalpara village, Sreepur upazila, Magura district. She is the daughter of Afsar Uddin Ahmed and Khurshida Parvin. She is a lawyer by profession.

In the 8th Parliament she was a BNP-nominated member of parliament for women's seat 38. Her name was on the BNP's announced list of 36 for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament as a former member of parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-5 through the votes of the members of parliament.
প্রফেসর ড. মোঃ ইলিয়াস মোল্লা ফরিদপুর-১:
Professor Dr Md. Elias Molla is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Faridpur-1 (Madhukhali, Boalmari and Alfadanga). This is his first term in Parliament, as the nominee of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. He is an academic and a former chairman of the Department of Chemistry at Jahangirnagar University.

He was born in Kalpoha village, Kamaldia Union, Madhukhali Upazila, Faridpur District. His father is Abdul Majid Molla and his mother Saleha Begum. He is the second of five siblings. He won talent-pool scholarships in Class 5 and Class 8, and passed his SSC and HSC in the first division with letter marks.

From the Department of Chemistry at Jahangirnagar University he came first in the first class in his bachelor's (Hons) examination and obtained a first class in his MSc. In 1981 he joined the same university as a lecturer. Awarded a Commonwealth Scholarship in 1984, he obtained his PhD from the University of Sussex, England, in 1987, and he received the Hariprasanna Gold Medal from the University of Dhaka. In 1992 he carried out postdoctoral research in England on a Royal Society of Chemistry fellowship; in 1993 he was promoted to professor; and from 1995 to 1997 he carried out postdoctoral research for a second time, at the University of Bayreuth in Germany, on an Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship. From 2012 to 2015 he was chairman of the Department of Chemistry at Jahangirnagar University. About 100 of his research papers have been published in national and international journals, and many students have obtained doctorates under his supervision.

He has been associated with Islami Chhatra Shibir since its founding in 1977 and was the second president of its Jahangirnagar University branch. He is currently a member of the Shura and of the executive council of Jamaat-e-Islami's Dhaka District branch.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Faridpur-1 with 154,145 votes under the scales symbol.
ফকির মাহবুব আনাম স্বপন ডাক, টেলিযোগাযোগ:
Faqir Mahbub Anam Swapan is the Minister of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and Minister of Science and Technology, and the member of parliament (MP) for Tangail-1. He took charge of the two ministries on 17 February 2026. A businessman, Swapan is a member of the BNP's national executive committee.

He was born on 5 March 1953; his father is Mokbul Hossain Faqir.

In the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament he was elected MP for the first time, as the BNP candidate for Tangail-1, with 137,433 votes; his nearest rival, the Jamaat-e-Islami candidate, received 94,462 votes. After the election he was given charge of the country's posts, telecommunications, information technology, and science and technology sectors.
ফখর উদ্দিন আহমেদ ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে ম:
Fakhar Uddin Ahmed is the member of parliament for Mymensingh-11 (Bhaluka Upazila) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). Locally he is known as Fakhar Uddin Ahmed Bachchu.

He was born on 11 April 1970 in Bhaluka Upazila, Mymensingh District. He is the son of Md. Afaz Uddin Bepari and Mst. Hamida Khatun. He is a businessman by profession.

He has been involved in BNP politics for a long time. In the party he has served as a member of the Central Executive Committee, joint convener of Mymensingh South District BNP, and president and convener of Bhaluka Upazila BNP. In November 2025 the party nominated him for Mymensingh-11.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected with 111,230 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.
ফরহাদ হোসেন আজাদ পানি সম্পদ প্রতিমন্ত্রী:
Forhad Hossain Azad is the State Minister for Water Resources and the member of parliament for Panchagarh-2. He took office on 17 February 2026. Azad, the BNP's rural development affairs secretary, has been elected to Parliament for the first time, in the 13th Parliament.

He was born on 12 March 1966 in Menagram, in Panchpir union of Boda upazila, Panchagarh; his father is Md. Tozammel Hossain. After taking a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Dhaka, he went abroad for higher education and pursued specialised studies in international relations and development economics.

He entered politics in 1991. He has served as the BNP's central rural development affairs secretary and as member secretary of the Panchagarh district BNP. After winning the Panchagarh-2 seat with the sheaf of paddy symbol in the 2026 election, he joined Tarique Rahman's Cabinet. He is the father of one son.
ফারজানা শারমিন পুতুল সমাজকল্যাণ প্রতিমন্:
Farzana Sharmin Putul is the State Minister for Social Welfare and the member of parliament (MP) for Natore-1. She has held this office since 4 March 2026. A Supreme Court lawyer, Putul was a member of the interim government's Anti-Corruption Commission Reform Commission, and is a special assistant on the BNP chairperson's foreign affairs advisory committee.

She was born on 2 November 1984. Her father, Fazlur Rahman Potol, was State Minister for Youth and Sports and for Communications, and a four-time MP for Natore-1; her mother was a teacher at Ideal Laboratory School and College in Mirpur. Her family home is at Gouripur in Lalpur upazila of Natore. She graduated in law from the University of Dhaka and the University of London, and obtained two postgraduate degrees, from the University of Dhaka and from BPP University College in London.

She enrolled as a lawyer in the district court in 2008 and in the Supreme Court in 2012. She specialises in criminal cases, judicial review and constitutional law. After working at Barrister Moudud Ahmed & Associates, she is now a partner at Rights Chambers; she is legal adviser to various banks, insurance companies and private organisations, and a lawyer for the BTRC (Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission). She is on the British High Commission's list of approved English-speaking lawyers, and is a member of the International Bar Association, Middle Temple and the Asian Society of International Law.

She also works with the BNP's human rights committee and media cell. On behalf of BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, she conducted a case challenging the Fifteenth Amendment to the Constitution. In the 13th parliamentary election in 2026 she was elected MP for the first time, from her father's seat, Natore-1.
ফাহমিদা হক ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক্ষি:
Fahmida Haq is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-18 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Fahmida Haq was born on 1 March 1978. She is the daughter of Zahirul Haque and Shirin Haque. She holds a BSc. She is a writer and analyst by profession.

Her husband, Zillur Rahman, is the presenter of the television talk show Tritiyo Matra. Fahmida Haq is one of the 36 people the BNP nominated for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-18 through the votes of the members of parliament.
ফাহিমা নাসরিন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক:
Fahima Nasrin is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-29 in the 13th Parliament. Nominated by the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party), she is the party's assistant international affairs secretary and a member of its central executive committee. In Parliament she is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Women and Children Affairs.

Also known as Fahima Nasrin Munni, she was born on 25 December 1963. Her father is the late Abul Hashem Mia and her mother is the late Rabeya Khatun. She is the wife of Ali Askar Qureshi of Deosar village, Rampal union, Munshiganj Sadar upazila.

She is a lawyer of the Supreme Court by profession. She served as a deputy attorney general during the BNP government. She was elected senior vice-president of the Supreme Court Bar Association.
