This veteran leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has been elected member of parliament for the fifth time. He is a former Whip of Parliament and an organiser of the Liberation War.

Shahjahan Chowdhury was born on 31 December 1952 in Rajapalong union, Ukhia upazila, Cox's Bazar district. His father, Abul Kashem Chowdhury, was chairman of the undivided Rajapalong union parishad; his mother is Begum Nur Jahan Chowdhury. After completing his primary and secondary education in Ukhia, he passed the intermediate examination from Chittagong College, and in 1975 he completed a BA (Honours) in sociology at the University of Chittagong.

He has been active in politics since his school days. During the Liberation War, as president of the Ukhia thana Chhatra League, he played an active part on the side of the Liberation War. According to accounts in various books, in December 1971 news of a plan to move the weapons out of Ukhia police station reached the freedom fighters through him, and on that basis the Ukhia police station operation was carried out on 12 December.

In 1977 he was elected chairman of the Rajapalong union parishad. A founding joint convener of the BNP in what was then Cox's Bazar subdivision, Shahjahan Chowdhury later served two terms as president of the Cox's Bazar district BNP. In the election to the 2nd Parliament in 1979 he was first elected member of parliament, from what was then Chattogram-18 (Ramu, Ukhia and Teknaf), and in the 2nd Parliament he was a Whip of the ruling party. He was elected member of parliament for Cox's Bazar-4 in 1991, February 1996 and 2001. In the 5th Parliament he was a member of the all-party parliamentary committee formed to establish peace in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and of the committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs. In the 8th Parliament he was chair of the parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Housing and Public Works.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was again elected member of parliament for Cox's Bazar-4 as the BNP candidate, winning 123,582 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
শাহজাহান চৌধুরী ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে চট:
Shahjahan Chowdhury is the member of parliament for Chattogram-15 (Lohagara upazila and most of Satkania upazila) in the 13th Parliament. This leader of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has been elected member of parliament for the third time. He is a member of Jamaat's central executive council and a former ameer of the Chattogram metropolitan unit. In Parliament he is a member of the Committee on Private Members' Bills and Private Members' Resolutions.

Shahjahan Chowdhury was born in Chhamdar Para, Satkania, Chattogram district. He is the son of Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury.

He completed his primary education at Satkania Chhamdar Para Primary School and his secondary education at Satkania Model High School. He then obtained a Diploma in Commerce from Chittagong Government Polytechnic Institute and passed the B.Com from Government City College, Chittagong. He later obtained an LLB degree. He is a businessman by profession.

He was first elected member of parliament in the election to the 5th Parliament in 1991. In the election to the 8th Parliament in 2001 he was elected for the second time, from Chattogram-14.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-15 as the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami candidate, winning 181,238 votes.
শিরীন সুলতানা ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক:
Sherin Sultana is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-2 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is self-reliance affairs secretary of the BNP central committee. In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Sherin Sultana was born on 3 May 1967. She is the daughter of Abdul Motaleb and Fouzia Akter. She is a businesswoman by profession.

She is a former general secretary of the Mohila Dal. In 2001 she was a BNP member of parliament for a reserved women's seat in the 8th Parliament. Her name was second on the BNP's final list of 36 for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-2 through the votes of the members of parliament.

Her husband, BNP joint secretary general Khairul Kabir Khokon, is the member of parliament for Narsingdi-1. The couple are thus both members of the same Parliament.
শেখ জাহাঙ্গীর হুসাইন হেলাল ত্রয়োদশ জাতী:
Sk. Zahangir Hossain Helal is the member of parliament (MP) for Khulna-2 in the 13th Parliament. He entered Parliament for the first time as the nominee of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. He is a member of Jamaat-e-Islami's central Majlis-e-Shura and serves as secretary general of its Khulna metropolitan unit.

He was born on 21 November 1974 in Khulna. He is the son of S.M. Mujibur Rahman and Hosneara Begum.

He completed his honours and master's degrees at Government Brajalal (BL) College in Khulna and later obtained an LLB degree. In his professional life he has been providing legal assistance to ordinary people as a lawyer at the Khulna Judge Court.

As a student he was involved with Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir and served as president of its Khulna metropolitan unit. He also has experience in local government: he served as councillor for Ward 31 of Khulna City Corporation.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Khulna-2 with 93,789 votes on the scales symbol.
শেখ ফরিদ আহম্মেদ ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে চ:
Sk Farid Ahmed is the member of parliament for Chandpur-3 (Chandpur Sadar and Haimchar upazilas) in the 13th Parliament. He has come to Parliament for the first time, from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

Farid Ahmed was born on 1 June 1965 in Shahid Rehanbag village, Chandpur Sadar upazila. He is the son of Sheikh Momtaz Uddin and Begum Roushan Akter. He obtained a BA (bachelor's) degree from the University of Dhaka.

In his professional life he is managing director of the Silkways Group. In politics he has long been in the leadership of Chandpur district BNP. In 2010 he became general secretary of the district BNP, in 2014 he was made convener for the district, and in 2023 he was elected president of Chandpur district BNP.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament, winning 165,404 votes in Chandpur-3 with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
শেখ ফরিদুল ইসলাম পরিবেশ, বন ও জলবায়ু পর:
Shaikh Faridul Islam is the State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the member of parliament (MP) for Bagerhat-3. He took office on 17 February 2026. A politician who has carried out research on climate change in the Sundarbans, he was elected for the first time, to the 13th Parliament.

He was born on 3 January 1970 in the village of Bardia in Banshtali Union, Rampal upazila, Bagerhat; his father, S.K. Abdur Rahman, is a businessman, and his mother is Shakhina Begum. After primary education in the village, he passed the SSC from Baintala Kashipur High School in 1984 and the HSC from Abul Kalam College in Rampal in 1986. He obtained a BA (Honours) and an MA from the Department of Philosophy at the University of Dhaka. In 2012 he earned a PhD in environmental science from American World University in California, United States; the subject of his research was "Climate change in the Sundarbans of Bangladesh and its impact on livelihoods".

Alongside politics, he is involved in free eye-care programmes. Having won Bagerhat-3 as the BNP candidate in the 2026 election, he was given charge of the environment and climate ministry as a representative of the Sundarbans region.
শেখ মজিবুর রহমান ইকবাল ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় স:
Sk. Mozibur Rahman Iqbal is the member of parliament for Kishoreganj-5 (Nikli and Bajitpur Upazilas) in the 13th Parliament. Elected as an independent candidate, he has entered Parliament for the first time.

Iqbal was born on 12 October 1963 in Teghoria village, Bajitpur Upazila, Kishoreganj District. He is the son of Nazibur Rahman and Syeda Hajera Khatun. He is a businessman by profession.

He was involved in BNP politics for a long time, serving as president of Bajitpur Upazila BNP and as a member of the BNP Central Executive Committee.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as an independent candidate with 79,604 votes. He is married to Sathi Rahman and is the father of two sons.
শেখ মনজুরুল হক (রাহাদ) ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় স:
Shaikh Monzurul Haque Rahad is the member of parliament (MP) for Bagerhat-2 in the 13th Parliament. Nominated by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, this young politician has entered Parliament for the first time. He serves as Bagerhat district president of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami's youth department.

He was born in Bagerhat Sadar upazila. He is the son of Shaikh Mokhtar Ali and Sufia Begum, and is the youngest of three siblings.

Rahad received his primary education at Bagerhat Government High School and completed his secondary education at Rotary Secondary School. He then passed his higher secondary examination from Government Majid Memorial City College and obtained bachelor's and master's degrees in accounting from Bagerhat Government Prafulla Chandra College. He is a businessman by profession. In 2011 he took part in a local election.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Bagerhat-2 with 117,709 votes on the scales symbol.
শেখ মোঃ রেজাউল ইসলাম ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংস:
Sk. Md. Rejaul Islam is the member of parliament (MP) in the 13th Parliament for Naogaon-6, a seat made up of Raninagar and Atrai upazilas. He entered Parliament for the first time as the candidate nominated by the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party). Locally he is known as Sheikh Rejaul Islam Reju.

He was born on 13 May 1959 in Atrai upazila of Naogaon district. His father's name is Sheikh Munsur Rahman and his mother's name is Nurun Nahar Begum. By profession he is engaged in agriculture and business.

Rejaul Islam has led the Atrai upazila BNP for more than eighteen years and is president of the upazila BNP. In 2025 he also served as joint convener of the Naogaon district BNP. Local media have reported his involvement in humanitarian assistance in the area during various disasters, including the coronavirus pandemic, and in development work for schools, colleges, mosques, madrasas and temples.

The party nominated him as its candidate for Naogaon-6 while he was president of the Atrai upazila BNP. In the 13th parliamentary election on 12 February 2026 he was elected with 108,866 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol. The Jamaat-e-Islami candidate for the seat, Md. Khabirul Islam, received 97,629 votes.
শেখ রবিউল আলম সড়ক পরিবহন ও সেতু, রেলপথ:
Shaikh Rabiul Alam is the Minister for Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping, and the member of parliament for Dhaka-10. On 17 February 2026 he took charge of these three ministries of the country's communications sector. A businessman, Rabiul Alam is managing director of the real estate company Pleasant Properties Limited.

He was born on 6 October 1971 in Mollahat, Bagerhat; his father is Shaikh Lokman Hakim. He studied in the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism at the University of Dhaka.

A member of the BNP National Executive Committee, Rabiul Alam was the party's candidate for Dhaka-10 in the 2018 election. In the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament he was elected member of parliament for the first time, from the same seat, with 80,436 votes.
সরওয়ার জামাল নিজাম ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদ:
Sarwar Jamal Nizam is the member of parliament for Chattogram-13 (Anwara and Karnaphuli upazilas) in the 13th Parliament. This experienced politician of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has been elected member of parliament for the fourth time.

Sarwar Jamal Nizam was born in Chattogram. He is the son of Alhaj Habibur Rahman and Alhajjani Anwara Nizam. Vice Admiral Sarwar Jahan Nizam of the Bangladesh Navy is his brother.

On the BNP's nomination he was elected member of parliament three times in a row from the then Chattogram-12 seat, in the elections to the 6th Parliament in February 1996, the 7th Parliament in June 1996 and the 8th Parliament in 2001. Within the party he is a member of the BNP executive committee.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-13 as the BNP candidate, winning 126,192 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
সরদার মোঃ সাখাওয়াত হোসেন বকুল স্বাস্থ্য:
Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain Bakul is Minister for Health and Family Welfare and MP for Narsingdi-4 (Monohardi-Belabo). He was sworn in as minister on 17 February 2026. A freedom fighter of 1971, Bakul has been elected MP from this seat four times.

He was born in 1951 into the Sardar family of Hafizpur village, Chalakchar Union, Monohardi Upazila, Narsingdi; his father is Sardar Asmat Ali. He studied at Chalakchar High School, Narsingdi Government College and the University of Dhaka, and was GS (general secretary) of the Narsingdi Government College students' union. While a student at the University of Dhaka he took an active part in the Liberation War.

He began his political career in the Chhatra Union and later joined the BNP. He has served as senior vice-president of the Narsingdi District BNP, convener of the Monohardi Upazila BNP and president of the upazila Muktijoddha Sangsad (freedom fighters' council).

He won Narsingdi-4 in the elections of 1991, February 1996 and 2001; in one of these his opponent was the Awami League candidate, former army chief Lieutenant General (retd) Nuruddin Khan. In the 2026 election he was elected MP for the fourth time with 161,912 votes.
সরদার সরফুদ্দিন আহমেদ, যিনি সান্টু নামে:
Sarder Sharfuddin Ahmed, known as Santu, is the member of parliament (MP) for Barishal-2 (Wazirpur and Banaripara) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Land. He was born on 4 February 1946. He is the son of Alhaj A. Mazid Mia and Alhaj Maleka Begum.

Sharfuddin Ahmed is a member of the BNP's central executive committee. Before the election he was joint convener of Barishal district BNP and convener of Wazirpur upazila BNP. He has played a part in founding educational, service and religious institutions. At Guthia in Barishal he built the Baitul Aman Jame Mosque, which was inaugurated on 16 December 2003. The mosque complex also includes an eidgah, a madrasa and a graveyard. He is also known for humanitarian initiatives during disasters. In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Barishal-2 with 141,622 votes on the sheaf of paddy symbol.
সরোয়ার আলমগীর ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে চট্:
Sarowar Alamgir is the member of parliament for Chattogram-2 (Fatikchhari) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

Alongside politics, Sarowar Alamgir is a businessman. He is the founder and chief executive officer of Halda Group, a Chattogram-based industrial group. Founded in the mid-1990s, the group works in ready-made garments, garment accessories, textile manufacturing and real estate.

As a member of the BNP he has taken part in various political activities of the party in Chattogram. In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he won the Chattogram-2 seat as the BNP candidate, receiving 138,545 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol. After the gazette of the results was published, he took the oath as a member of parliament on 9 July 2026.
সাইদ উদ্দিন আহমাদ হানজালা মাদারীপুর-১ (শ:
Sayed Uddin Ahmad Hanzala is a Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis member of parliament elected from Madaripur-1 (Shibchar). This Islamic scholar, known as Pirzada Hanzala, is representing the seat in Parliament for the first time, in the 13th Parliament. In Parliament he is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology.

Hanzala was born on 24 March 1997 in Bahadurpur village, Shibchar Upazila, Madaripur District. His father is Mubin Uddin Ahmad and his mother Ruhana Ahmed. He is a seventh-generation descendant of Haji Shariatullah.

After memorising the Quran (hifz) at a local madrasa, he studied under the Madani Nisab curriculum in Dhaka. He later completed the Dawra-e-Hadith at Madrasatul Arabia Al Islamia Darul Uloom in Azaadville, Africa. He is an Islamic scholar by profession.

Hanzala is a member of the central executive committee of Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis. In the 13th parliamentary election of 2026, standing as the candidate of the 11-party electoral alliance under the rickshaw symbol, he won with a total of 64,909 votes, by a margin of 385 votes.
সাঈদ আল নোমান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে চট্ট:
Sayeed Al Noman is the member of parliament for Chattogram-10 (the Double Mooring, Pahartali and Khulshi areas) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and of the Library Committee, and chair of Sub-committee No. 5 of the Library Committee. In June 2026 the Speaker nominated him a member of the Senate of the University of Chittagong.

Sayeed Al Noman was born on 22 December 1979. His father is Abdullah Al Noman, a former vice-chairman of the BNP and former minister, who was a member of parliament from the same area. His mother is Tasmin Ara Begum.

He obtained a bachelor's degree from Central Michigan University in the United States, a master's degree from the London School of Economics and Political Science and an MPhil from St Cross College, University of Oxford. In 2006, together with his father, he founded East Delta University in Chattogram, and he is vice-chairman of the university's board of trustees.

He became more active in politics after the July uprising of 2024. During the election campaign he went to voters in markets, at tea stalls and from neighbourhood to neighbourhood, pledging to build Chattogram into a hub of skilled young people, to create jobs and to provide modern civic services. In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-10, winning 122,978 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
সাঈদ আহমেদ শরীয়তপুর-১ আসন থেকে নির্বাচি:
Sayeed Ahmed is a Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) member of parliament elected from Shariatpur-1. Known as Sayeed Ahmed Aslam, this businessman and politician is representing the seat in Parliament for the first time, in the 13th Parliament.

He was born on 3 January 1962 in Damudya Upazila, Shariatpur District. His father is Md. Ali Akbar Mia and his mother Syeda Safia Akbar.

In his professional life he is an established businessman. He is the proprietor of Ahmed Shipping Lines, Ahmed Inland Shipping Agency, A K International and Ahmed Airways Services. He also serves as chairman of Global Insurance Limited.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP as the BNP candidate with 77,398 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol.
সাচিং প্রু জেরী পার্বত্য চট্টগ্রাম বিষয়:
Saching Prue Jerry is the Minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs and the member of parliament for the hill district seat of Bandarban. He has been in charge of this ministry since August 2026. A member of the royal family of the Bohmong Circle, Jerry belongs to the Marma Buddhist community; he is convener of the Bandarban district BNP and a member of the party's national executive committee.

His father, Aung Shwe Prue Chowdhury, was the Bohmong Raja. His maternal uncle's wife, Ma Mya Ching, was a member of the 5th and 6th Parliaments from a reserved women's seat.

He was first elected member of parliament for the Bandarban hill district seat in the election to the 6th Parliament in 1996. He has also served as chairman of the Bandarban Sadar upazila parishad and of the Bandarban Hill District Council. Winning by a wide margin in the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament, he entered Parliament for the second time and was given charge of the ministry for the affairs of the three hill districts.
সানজিদা ইসলাম ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক:
Sanjida Islam is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-16 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Known as Sanjida Islam Tuli, she was born on 8 March 1983. She passed her secondary and higher secondary examinations from BAF Shaheen College Dhaka. She then obtained a bachelor's degree in textile engineering from Bangladesh University of Textiles.

Sanjida Islam is a human rights activist and a coordinator of Mayer Daak. In 2025 she was nominated for the international Human Rights Tulip award for her human rights work.

In the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament she contested Dhaka-14. The BNP later nominated her for a reserved women's seat, and she became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-16 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সাবিকুন্নাহার ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক:
Subikunnahar is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-39 in the 13th Parliament. Nominated by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, she is law and human rights secretary of the party's women's wing and a member of its central executive council. In Parliament she is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Women and Children Affairs.

Known as Advocate Subikunnahar Munni, the lawyer was born on 1 January 1973 in Dhaka. Her father is Md. Abu Sayed and her mother is Rowshan Sayeed.

She completed her higher secondary education at Begum Badrunnesa Government Women's College and her bachelor's and master's degrees at the University of Dhaka. She is a lawyer of the Supreme Court by profession. She is also serving as secretary of the women's wing of the Bangladesh Lawyers' Council.

As a student she was central president of Bangladesh Islami Chhatri Sangstha.

Subikunnahar Munni was one of the 13 people whose names the 11-party electoral alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami announced on 20 April 2026 for the reserved seats for women. As the only candidate for this seat, which is filled by a vote of members of parliament, she was elected unopposed, and the Election Commission published the gazette on 30 April 2026.
সালাহ উদ্দিন, যিনি সালাহউদ্দিন আইউবী নাম:
Salah Uddin, known as Salahuddin Ayubi, is a member of the 13th Parliament elected from Gazipur-4 (Kapasia). This is his first term in Parliament, as the nominee of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. He is a member of Jamaat's central Majlis-e-Shura and deputy ameer (naib-e-ameer) of its Gazipur Metropolitan unit.

He was born on 2 March 1987 in Belashi village, Rayed Union, Gazipur District. His father is Maulana Imam Uddin and his mother Asma Akter.

He has received higher education in both the general and the madrasa streams. He completed his Dakhil at Rayed Darus Sunnah Dakhil Madrasa, his Alim and Fazil at Mohakhali Darul Ulum Hossainia Kamil Madrasa, and his Kamil at Dhaka Alia Madrasa. He also obtained a bachelor's (Hons) degree in English language and literature from Dhaka College, a master's degree from World University of Bangladesh and an LLB degree from the National University. He is a teacher by profession.

In 2021 he served as central president of Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Gazipur-4 with 101,779 votes under the scales symbol.
সালাহউদ্দিন আহমদ স্বরাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী এবং ক:
Salahuddin Ahmed is the Minister for Home Affairs and the member of parliament for Cox's Bazar-1 (Chakaria–Pekua). He took office as minister on 17 February 2026. A lawyer and former government official, he is a member of the BNP's national standing committee and has also served as the party's spokesperson.

He was born on 30 June 1962 in Sikderpara village, Pekua, Cox's Bazar; his father is Moulvi Saidul Haque and his mother Begum Ayesha Haque. He passed the SSC from Shilkhali High School in Pekua in 1977 and the HSC from Chittagong Government College in 1979. After obtaining a bachelor's (honours) degree in law from the University of Dhaka in 1984 and a master's degree in 1986, he was enrolled as a lawyer. As a student he was a central vice-president of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and for a time its acting president.

Having passed the 7th BCS examination, he joined the administration cadre in 1988, and in 1991 he became assistant private secretary to Prime Minister Khaleda Zia. In January 1996 he left government service to enter active politics, and he won the Cox's Bazar-1 seat three times in a row, in both elections of that year and in 2001. On 10 October 2001 he became State Minister for Communications; he was the first minister from Cox's Bazar district since independence. Pekua was formed as a separate upazila in 2002 on his initiative. He was president of the Cox's Bazar district BNP, and in 2010 he was elected a central joint secretary general of the party.

From February 2007 he was imprisoned for about two years and two months under the caretaker government; during that time his wife, Advocate Hasina Ahmed, won the Cox's Bazar-1 seat in the 2008 election. In March 2015, while he was the party's spokesperson, he went missing from Uttara in Dhaka; about two months later, on 11 May, he was found in Shillong, in Meghalaya, India. In the case filed there for illegal entry, an Indian court acquitted him in 2018, and on 28 February 2023 the appellate court upheld that verdict. He was elected a member of the BNP's national standing committee while he was still abroad.
সুলতান সালাউদ্দিন টুকু মৎস্য ও প্রাণিসম্:
Sultan Salauddin Tuku is the State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock and the member of parliament (MP) for Tangail-5. He has been in charge of this ministry since 4 March 2026; before that, from 17 February to 4 March, he was State Minister for Agriculture and Food.

He was born in Tangail in 1971; his father is Md. Mohiuddin Mia.

A leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, Tuku was elected MP for Tangail-5 for the first time in the 2026 election to the 13th Parliament.
সুলতানা আহমেদ ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক:
Sultana Ahmed is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-17 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Land.

Sultana Ahmed was born on 26 February 1964. She is the daughter of M. N. Kazi and Nilufa Kazi. She is a businesswoman by profession.

She is active in the leadership of the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal and has been a member of parliament before. Her name was on the BNP's announced list of 36 for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament as a former member of parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-17 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সুলতানা জেসমিন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংর:
Sultana Jesmen is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-49 in the 13th Parliament. The alliance of independent MPs nominated her for this seat, and she is that alliance's only MP in a reserved seat. In Parliament she is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

Known as Sultana Jesmen Jui, she was born on 23 February 1991 in Buichakathi village, Sekhmatia union, Nazirpur upazila, Pirojpur. Her father is Abdul Aziz Howlader and her mother is Amina Begum.

She is a former student of the University of Dhaka. According to Wikipedia, she completed a bachelor's degree in Islamic Studies there and a master's degree in project management at a university in China. Professionally she works in the research and consultancy sector.

In student politics she served in the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal as a member of its central executive committee, as assistant general secretary and as vice-president. From 2022 to 2024 she was convener of the Zia Memorial Library.

In April 2026 her nomination papers were submitted on behalf of the independent alliance with the signatures of the MPs for Kishoreganj-5 and Mymensingh-1. As the only candidate for this seat, which is filled by a vote of members of parliament, she was elected unopposed, and the Election Commission published the gazette on 30 April 2026.
সূবর্না সিকদার ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংর:
Subarna Sikder is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-20 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Subarna Sikder was born on 20 July 1973. She is the daughter of Anil Krishna Sikder and Sova Rani Sikder. She is a former teacher and a leader of the Matua community.

Subarna Sikder is one of the 36 people the BNP nominated for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament, as a representative of the minority communities. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-20 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সেলিনা সুলতানা ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংর:
Salina Sultana is the member of parliament (MP) for reserved Women's Seat-35 in the 13th Parliament. The BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) nominated her for this seat.

Known as Salina Sultana Nishita, she was born on 2 January 1979. Her father is the late Ali Newaz Sarkar and her mother is Rabeya Sarkar. Having risen through student politics, she is a former joint general secretary of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal. A Bangla Tribune report named her among the former Chhatra Dal leaders who were recognised on the BNP's list for the reserved seats.

Salina Sultana was one of the 36 people whose names the BNP announced on 20 April 2026 for the reserved seats for women. As the only candidate for this seat, which is filled by a vote of members of parliament, she was elected unopposed, and the Election Commission published the gazette on 30 April 2026.
সেলিমা রহমান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক্:
Selima Rahman is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-1 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is a member of the BNP's national standing committee. In Parliament she chairs the standing committee on the Ministry of Women and Children Affairs.

Selima Rahman was born on 1 September 1941 in Baherchar Khudrakathi village, Babuganj upazila, Barishal district. Her father, Justice Abdul Jabbar Khan, was a former Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan; her mother is Saleha Khatun. Her brothers and sisters include the journalist and columnist Sadeque Khan, the poet Abu Zafar Obaidullah, the journalist and former minister A.Z.M. Enayetullah Khan, and Shahidullah Khan Badal, publisher of the newspaper New Age.

In the BNP she has served as joint secretary general and as vice-chairman. She was a member of parliament from 2001 to 2006, and during that time she served as State Minister for Cultural Affairs.

Selima Rahman is one of the 36 people the BNP nominated for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-1 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সৈয়দ আবদুল্লাহ মোহাম্মদ তাহের ত্রয়োদশ:
Syed Abdullah Mohammed Taher is the member of parliament for Cumilla-11 (Chauddagram upazila) in the 13th Parliament. He has come to Parliament for the second time, from Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, and is Deputy Leader of the Opposition in Parliament. In Parliament he is chair of the standing committee on public accounts. He is also a member of several committees, including the Business Advisory Committee and the standing committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In the party he is a nayeb-e-ameer (deputy ameer), international affairs secretary and a member of the central executive council.

Dr Taher was born into a Syed family in West Dekra village, Alkara union, Chauddagram upazila, Cumilla. His father was an Islamic preacher and scholar; his mother is Aksire Jahan Chowdhurani. As a student Taher won government talent-pool scholarships in class five and class eight, and came third in the SSC examination of the greater Cumilla board. After passing the HSC from Chittagong College in 1975, he obtained an MBBS degree from Dhaka Medical College. As a student he was the elected general secretary of the Dhaka Medical College students' union.

A physician by profession, Taher is associated with various institutions in the healthcare sector. He is the founding chairman of Central Medical College in Cumilla and chairman of Cumilla Tower Hospital and of Al Manar Hospital in Dhaka. He is also the founder of the monthly magazine for children and teenagers Notun Kishorkantha.

He became involved in student politics in his college years. In Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir he served as president of the Dhaka Medical College unit and of the Dhaka city unit, as central general secretary, and as central president for the 1985–86 and 1986–87 sessions. Internationally, from 1988 to 1992 he was Asia director of the International Islamic Federation of Student Organizations (IIFSO), and from 1992 to 1998 its secretary general. During the same period he was director for the Asian region of the World Assembly of Muslim Youth (WAMY). In the 8th parliamentary election in 2001 he was elected a member of parliament for the first time, from what was then the Cumilla-12 seat.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the second time, winning 133,308 votes in Cumilla-11 as the Jamaat-e-Islami candidate. His wife, Professor Dr Habiba Akter Chowdhury, is a radiology specialist. The couple have three daughters and a son.
সৈয়দ জয়নুল আবেদীন ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদ:
Syed Joynul Abedin is the member of parliament for Dhaka-4 (wards 47, 51, 52, 53, 54, 58 and 59 of Dhaka South City Corporation) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, nominated by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. In Parliament he is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Finance and the Standing Committee on Public Accounts. In the party he is a member of the Majlis-e-Shura and the working council of Dhaka Metropolitan South Jamaat.

Joynul Abedin was born on 1 March 1971 in Bakerganj, Barishal District. He is the son of Syed Hossain Ali and Rahela Begum. He obtained bachelor's and master's degrees with first class from the Department of Islamic Studies at Bangladesh Islami University. Professionally he was associated with the banking sector.

He has long been involved in Jamaat-e-Islami's political and organisational activities and has been active in party work in various areas of Dhaka city.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as Jamaat-e-Islami's nominated candidate with 77,367 votes under the scales symbol.

He has also taken initiatives in education and social service. He founded Talimul Millat Islamia Madrasa, Cordova International School, and Khondoker Gias Uddin Jamea Darul Arqam and Orphanage. During natural disasters and the coronavirus pandemic he delivered food and medical assistance to vulnerable people in his area.
সৈয়দ জাহাঙ্গীর আলম ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদ:
Syed Jahangir Alam is the member of parliament for Dinajpur-3 (Dinajpur Sadar) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), and is a member of the party's central executive committee. In Parliament he is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism. He had previously been elected mayor of Dinajpur Municipality for three consecutive terms.

Jahangir Alam was born on 24 February 1967 in Balubari, Dinajpur. His father is Syed Shamsul Alam Chowdhury and his mother Syeda Rizia Begum. He passed his SSC from Dinajpur Zilla School and his HSC from Dinajpur Adarsha College. He later obtained a bachelor's degree in commerce from Dinajpur Government College under the University of Rajshahi.

He joined Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal politics as a student. During the mass uprising of 1990 he was convener of the Dinajpur District All-Party Student Unity in the anti-Ershad movement. He later served as president and as general secretary of the Dinajpur district Chhatra Dal. In the parent party he was office secretary and youth affairs secretary of the Dinajpur district BNP. He has also served as convener of the district committee and vice-president of the central committee of the Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal, and as assistant organising secretary of the Rangpur divisional BNP. As mayor of Dinajpur Municipality from 2011 to 2023, he worked on local development, municipal administration and civic services.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected MP for Dinajpur-3, winning 140,608 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol. Alongside politics he is also involved in business. He is married to Nur Shamima Begum and is the father of two children.
হাফিজ উদ্দিন আহমদ বীর বিক্রম একজন বাংলাদ: Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram is a Bangladeshi politician and freedom fighter who was awarded the title of Bir Bikram for his heroic contribution to the Liberation War of 1971. He currently serves as Speaker of the 13th Parliament of Bangladesh.
হাফিজ উদ্দিন আহমদ বীর বিক্রম: পেশাগত জীব:
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram: a professional biography
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is well known for notable achievements in sport, as an army officer and in political leadership. His long career, from becoming a professional footballer in the 1960s to becoming Speaker of Parliament in 2026, is a unique example of steadfast commitment, determination and public service.

Early life and education
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad was born on 29 October 1944 into a respected Bengali Muslim family in Lalmohan, Bhola district. His father, Dr Azhar Uddin, was an influential political figure and a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan. His mother, Mst. Karimun Nesa, was a homemaker. In 1965 he obtained a master's degree (MA) in political science from the University of Dhaka, which laid the foundation for his later political life.

Contribution and success in sport
Before beginning his military and political life, he won particular fame as a footballer and was recognised as one of the most talented players of his time. A dynamic forward, he played for several leading clubs, including Mohammedan Sporting Club. He represented the Pakistan national football team from 1967 until Bangladesh gained independence in 1971. Internationally, he played matches in Iran, Turkey and Myanmar. Between 1964 and 1966 he set records in the 100 metres and 200 metres sprints in what was then East Pakistan. His extraordinary speed and competitive sporting skill took him to a distinguished position in South Asian football. In recognition of his contribution to football, FIFA awarded him its Centennial Order of Merit in 2005, one of the most prestigious honours in world sport.

Military contribution to Bangladesh's War of Independence
In Bangladesh's War of Independence in 1971, Hafiz Uddin Ahmad showed deep patriotism. A commissioned officer in the Pakistan Army, he took an active part in frontline combat while a captain in various strategically important sectors, especially in Sector 8 and under Z Force. On 30 March 1971, as an officer of the East Bengal Regiment, he declared a revolt against the Pakistan government at Jashore Cantonment. He then fought the Pakistani army for about eight hours and came out of the cantonment with two hundred soldiers. For his outstanding bravery and tactical skill he was awarded the Bir Bikram, Bangladesh's third-highest military award, which established him as a distinguished freedom fighter. His great sacrifice played a major role in the country's winning of independence. On 15 December 1971, after a day-long battle under Z Force, led by the then Major Ziaur Rahman, he captured Sylhet town.

Political life
Mr Hafiz was first elected MP for the Bhola-3 parliamentary constituency in 1986, and later, in 1992, he joined the BNP. In his parliamentary career he was elected MP to the 3rd (1986), 4th (1988), 5th (1991), 6th (1996), 7th (1996), 8th (2001) and 13th (2026) Parliaments. In his political life he took on party posts in the BNP and joined its standing committee, a reflection of his special standing in the party. He was later elected a member of the "National Standing Committee", the BNP's highest policymaking forum.
As a minister he has successfully held several important portfolios, including State Minister for Commerce (1996); Minister of Water Resources, Minister of Commerce and Minister of Jute (2001-2006); and, most recently, Minister of Liberation War Affairs (2026).
In March 2026 he was unanimously elected Speaker of the 13th Parliament of Bangladesh, and the Honourable President administered his oath. As Speaker of Parliament he presides over the sessions of Parliament in conducting parliamentary business, and continues to provide leadership at an important juncture in Bangladesh's democratic development.

Personal life and ideology
The distinguished educationist Dilara Hafiz was the wife of Hafiz Uddin Ahmad. Dilara Hafiz served as principal of Eden Mohila College, Dhaka, and of Shaheed Suhrawardy College, and as director general (DG) of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education. Dilara Hafiz died on 28 March 2026.
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is the father of two sons and one daughter. His son Shahrukh Hafiz is a computer engineer by profession and his son Taharat Hafiz is a businessman, and his daughter Shamama Shahrin Hafiz has completed an MBA at the University of Windsor in Canada. He is universally recognised for his discipline in his personal and sporting life, his military orderliness, his political experience and his integrity.
He is a devoted supporter of the core spirit of the War of Independence and has always spoken out for a strong democracy, institutional accountability, national development and the rule of law. His clear positions and candid views on contemporary issues have established him as a principled politician.

Achievements
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad's working life is a vast canvas of success in many fields: he is at once a FIFA-recognised footballer, a freedom fighter decorated with the Bir Bikram, a decorated military officer, a seven-time elected member of parliament and an experienced minister. Now serving as Speaker of Parliament, he has a career of more than six decades that reflects his commitment to national progress and shows a unique union of personal excellence and public service in Bangladesh's democratic evolution.
হাফেজ মুহাঃ রবিউল বাশার ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয়:
Hafez Muhammad Rabiul Bashar is the member of parliament (MP) for Satkhira-3 (Assasuni and Kaliganj) in the 13th Parliament. Known as Muhaddis Rabiul Bashar, he entered Parliament for the first time as the nominee of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. He is a member of Jamaat-e-Islami's central Majlis-e-Shura.

He was born on 1 February 1966 in the village of Majh Parulia in Debhata upazila, Satkhira district. He is the son of Abdul Latif Sardar and Anowara Khatun. He studied at the University of Dhaka and is engaged in teaching by profession.

In his organisational career, Rabiul Bashar has served as amir of the Satkhira district unit of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected MP for Satkhira-3 with 184,233 votes on the scales symbol. In this election, Jamaat-e-Islami candidates won all four seats in Satkhira.
হাবিবুর রশিদ হাবিব রেলপথ মন্ত্রণালয় এবং:
Habibur Rashid Habib is the State Minister for the Ministry of Railways and the Road Transport and Highways Division, and the member of parliament for Dhaka-9. On 17 February 2026 he was appointed State Minister for road, rail and water transport; after a reallocation of portfolios the following month he remained in charge of railways and road transport. A former general secretary of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, Habib is a member of the BNP Central Executive Committee.

He was born on 15 September 1973 in Belkuchi, Sirajganj, and spent his childhood there. After completing his secondary education at Motijheel Ideal School and his higher secondary education at Dhaka City College, he obtained a master's degree in management from Jagannath University.

He became involved in Chhatra Dal politics while studying at Dhaka City College. In 2010 he was convener of Chhatra Dal's Dhaka Metropolitan South unit. In April 2011 he survived being shot in the head and chest in an attack in Dhaka. In September 2012 he became central general secretary of Chhatra Dal, and from that year he was at the forefront of the movement against the then government. He later became joint general secretary of Dhaka Metropolitan South BNP.

During his years in opposition more than a hundred cases were filed against him, and he was jailed seven times, for nearly eight years in all. He has also done business as a contractor for the Public Works Department. In the 2026 election he was elected member of parliament for the first time, winning more than 51 per cent of the vote in Dhaka-9. His wife is Mabia Akter; they have three sons.
হামিদুর রহমান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে ঢাকা:
Hamidur Rahman is the member of parliament for Dhaka-7 (wards 23 to 33, 35 and 36 of Dhaka South City Corporation) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the Standing Committee on the Ministry of Commerce.

Hamidur Rahman was born on 20 January 1967. He is the son of Golap Rahman and Moriom Begum. He studied at Jagannath University. He is a businessman by profession.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026, he was elected as the BNP's nominated candidate with 104,666 votes under the sheaf of paddy symbol. In an interview before the election, he named tackling the constituency's gas shortage, sewerage problems and traffic congestion as his priorities.
হুমাম কাদের চৌধুরী ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Humam Quader Chowdhury is the member of parliament for Chattogram-7 (Rangunia upazila and the Sreepur-Kharandwip union of Boalkhali) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and of the Library Committee, and chair of Sub-committee No. 1 of the Library Committee.

Humam Quader Chowdhury was born into a political family on 23 June 1983. His father, Salahuddin Quader Chowdhury, was a member of the BNP standing committee and a member of parliament elected from various seats in Chattogram. His mother is Farhat Quader Chowdhury.

Continuing his family's political tradition, he became active in BNP politics and became known through party activities in the Chattogram region. He is a member of the BNP central executive committee.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-7 as the BNP candidate, winning 101,445 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
হুমায়ুন কবির টেকনোক্র্যাট কোটায় পররাষ্:
Humayun Kabir is State Minister for Foreign Affairs, appointed under the technocrat quota; he took the oath at Bangabhaban on 21 August 2026. Before that, from 17 February, he was Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Adviser on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief and the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, with the rank of a State Minister. Since 22 October 2025 he has been the BNP's joint secretary general for international affairs. He is not a member of parliament.

He was born on 2 October 1977 in Habashpur village, Umarpur union, Osmaninagar upazila, Sylhet. He moved to the United Kingdom as a child and was educated there. After taking a bachelor's (Honours) degree in international relations at the University of Sussex, he obtained three separate master's degrees from the London School of Economics, the University of Cambridge and Leeds Law School.

In the United Kingdom he worked as a strategy adviser in the Mayor of London's office and as a cabinet adviser in the office of the Executive Mayor of Lewisham. In the British government he served as a private secretary and special adviser in the Cabinet Office under Prime Minister Boris Johnson, and in the Ministry of Justice and the Wales Office under Rishi Sunak.

In the BNP he was a member of the advisory council of Tarique Rahman, then acting chairman, and his foreign affairs adviser. His responsibilities as State Minister were set on 23 August: political and diplomatic communication in bilateral relations, multilateral relations and United Nations affairs, and the interests of expatriate Bangladeshis. Shama Obaed Islam is also a State Minister in the same ministry; in the ministry's documents he is State Minister for Foreign Affairs-1.
হেলেন জেরিন খান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সং:
Helen Jerin Khan is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-9 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is assistant education affairs secretary of the BNP central committee. In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Commerce.

Helen Jerin Khan was born on 17 January 1969, into a politically aware family in Madaripur. She is the daughter of Abdul Latif Khan and Maksuda Khan. In her family, her father and paternal uncles were involved in politics, and her mother was a social worker.

In 1984 she passed the secondary examination from Charmugria Girls' School. In 1993 she obtained a bachelor's (honours) degree in Islamic history and culture from Eden Mohila College. She later obtained a master's degree in political science in 2010 and an LLB in 2012.

Her political journey began in her student days. She was a vice-president of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and was elected vice-president of the Eden Mohila College students' union. In 2005 she became a BNP member of parliament for a reserved women's seat. In the 2008 election she contested Madaripur-2 as the BNP candidate. She is also active in the organisational work of the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal. Her name was on the BNP's announced list for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament as a former member of parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-9 through the votes of the members of parliament.

She has lived in Madaripur and Dhaka. She is the mother of a daughter and a son.
